mcqs.explanation: The physical layer is guided by the protocols recognized by the ANSI and provides conversion to frames. The data link layer supports the simplified core functions specified by the OSI model like error detection.

mcqs.question: In frame relay networks, extended address is used ________

options.a: a) to increase the range of data link connection identifiers

mcqs.answer: a) to increase the range of data link connection identifiers
mcqs.explanation: Extended address is indicated by the last bit of every address byte in the DLCI. It specifies whether the byte is the last in the addressing field. It is used to increase the range of data link connection identifiers.

mcqs.question: What is FRAD in frame relay network?

options.a: a) FRAD assembles and disassembles the frames coming from other protocols
options.b: b) FRAD is used for modulation and demodulation
options.c: c) FRAD is used for error detection
options.d: d) FRAD is used for error recovery

mcqs.answer: a) FRAD assembles and disassembles the frames coming from other protocols
mcqs.explanation: FRAD stands for Frame Relay Assembler/Disassembler. It converts packets into frames that can be transmitted over Frame Relay Networks. It operates at the physical layer.

mcqs.question: What is a Frame Relay?

options.a: a) It is a set of protocols for data digital data transmission
options.b: b) It is a network bridge that communicates data bi-directionally
options.c: c) It is an access device that encapsulates data packets
options.d: d) It is a Wide Area Network (WAN) Technology that establishes virtual connection

mcqs.answer: d) It is a Wide Area Network (WAN) Technology that establishes virtual connection
mcqs.explanation: Frame Relay is based on Packet-Switching Technology. It is a WAN layer protocol and focuses on increasing its speed. It operates in the Physical and Data Link Layers of the OSI Model.

mcqs.question: In a Frame Relay network ____________ is a device that converts data packets into frames.
mcqs.explanation: Frame Relay Access Device or Frame Delay Assembler/Dissembler (FRAD) is a device that converts data packets into frames that can be sent over Frame Relay network. It also converts frames from Frame Relay into data packets. Whereas FRWAN stands for Frame relay WAN, VoFR stands for Voice over Frame Relay and FRS stands for Frame Relay Switch. Each of these entities carries out tasks that are different from FRAD.

mcqs.question: Frame Relay cannot support multiple users at the same time.
mcqs.explanation: Frame relay supports multiple users (or multiple circuits) on the same physical line using sub-interfaces, at the same time. It also establishes a permanent switch circuit.

links.context: This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “ACL”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following can be suited as a definition of an Access List?

options.a: a) Set of protocols to define traffic in a router
options.b: b) Set of rules used for packet filtering
options.c: c) Set of guidelines that every router should follow
options.d: d) Set of features that every router contains

mcqs.answer: b) Set of rules used for packet filtering
mcqs.explanation: An access control list is a set of confinements(rules), which can be configured in a router. These rules are defined to permit specific packets and to refuse particular packets at interface. ACL acts as a firewall at the router, which performs packet filtering.

mcqs.question: Which of the following set is used to identify Access Lists?

options.d: d) Special character and binary numbers

mcqs.explanation: We can assign names that suits our list so that we can remember them easily. Also, these named access lists are convenient to edit. Numbered access lists have specific number range to use and entries in these lists can’t be deleted.

mcqs.question: Which of the following aspects can’t be managed by a standard access list?
mcqs.explanation: Standard access list can’t deny or allow a particular service from the host. It can deal with a host or network or sub-network only. An extended access list can contain restrictions for the services that belong to different port numbers in a host.

mcqs.question: Which set of things will be taken into account in order to filter the packets in an extended access list?

options.a: a) Source IP address and destination IP address
options.b: b) Source IP address, protocol and port number
options.d: d) Source IP address, protocol, port number and destination IP address

mcqs.answer: d) Source IP address, protocol, port number and destination IP address
mcqs.explanation: In standard access list, only a destination IP address is used to filter, but in extended access list, source and destination IP address, protocol and port number are used. More specifications in packet filtering make extended access lists more sophisticated and advanced in security.

mcqs.question: One interface of a router can have multiple access lists.
mcqs.explanation: Each interface and protocol are allowed to have only one access list; also, multiple access lists for an interface causes ambiguity. But layer 2 devices can have multiple access lists for a single interface based on defined norms.

mcqs.question: What will happen if an empty access list is assigned to an interface?

options.a: a) It will allow all the packets into the network
options.b: b) It will deny all the packets from entering the network
options.c: c) It will allow only few packets into the network

mcqs.answer: a) It will allow all the packets into the network
mcqs.explanation: If there is no access list with the name that is assigned to the interface, then it can be considered as an empty access list. Empty access list clearly indicates that there are no restrictions on the packets. So, the interface will send all the packets into the network without restriction.

mcqs.question: What is the range of standard access list, if it is numbered?
mcqs.explanation: Both ranges help to identify whether specific access list is standard or extended. Standard access lists can also be represented by names, but unlike named lists, numbered access lists do not support modification like edit, or delete in them.

mcqs.question: What is the range of numbered extended access list?
mcqs.explanation: Given ranges will differ from numbered standard access list which has range from 1 to 99 or 1300 to 1999. Given ranges are used to distinguish the standard list and extended list.

mcqs.question: Which of the following cannot be an advantage of an access list?

options.b: b) It helps the network to perform well
options.c: c) It speeds up the packet transmission
options.d: d) It manages the traffic over the network

mcqs.answer: c) It speeds up the packet transmission
mcqs.explanation: An access list cannot speed up the packet transmission. An access list is nothing but a set of rules, which needs to be checked for a packet at the interface. So, the packet may take more time to be transmitted than usual time when it is subjected to checking.

mcqs.question: What is the main advantage of Port Access Control List?

options.a: a) It is implemented on layer 3 devices
options.b: b) It supports outbound and inbound traffic
options.c: c) It can have 2 access lists on a layer 2 interface
options.d: d) It can be configured on Ether-Channel also

mcqs.answer: c) It can have 2 access lists on a layer 2 interface
mcqs.explanation: Port access control list can be configured on layer 2 devices. As layer 2 deals with MAC and IP addresses, port access list supports both MAC access list and IP access list. So, a single interface can have 2 access lists in layer 2. Ether-Channels cannot configure port access control lists.

title: 7. Computer Network MCQ on TCP/IP Protocol Suite

links.context: This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “World Wide Web”.

mcqs.question: A piece of icon or image on a web page associated with another webpage is called ______
mcqs.explanation: URLs are locators for resources present on the World Wide Web. A plugin provides extra functionality to the webpage. An extension provides modification allowance for the core functionality of a webpage. Hyperlink is piece of icon or image on a web page associated with another webpage.

mcqs.question: Dynamic web page ______

options.a: a) is same every time whenever it displays
options.b: b) generates on demand by a program or a request from browser
options.c: c) both is same every time whenever it displays and generates on demand by a program or a request from browser
options.d: d) is different always in a predefined order

mcqs.answer: b) generates on demand by a program or a request from browser
mcqs.explanation: A dynamic web page provides different content every time the user opens it based on some events like new additions or time of the day. Languages such as JavaScript are used to respond to client-side events while languages such as PHP as used to respond to server-side events.

mcqs.question: What is a web browser?

options.a: a) a program that can display a web page
options.b: b) a program used to view html documents
options.c: c) it enables user to access the resources of internet

mcqs.explanation: A web browser is an application program that is used to access the World Wide Web resources, applications and websites. Some examples of web browsers are Google Chrome, Internet Explorer and Safari.

mcqs.question: Common gateway interface is used to _______

options.a: a) generate executable files from web content by web server

mcqs.answer: a) generate executable files from web content by web server
mcqs.explanation: CGI is an interface through servers can run execute console-based executable files on a web server that generates dynamic web pages. A CGI script executes only when a request is made. The script then generates HTML.

mcqs.question: URL stands for ________
mcqs.explanation: The Uniform Resource Locator is a locator for the resource to be located by HTTP on the World Wide Web. The URL is derived from the Uniform Resource Identifier.

mcqs.question: A web cookie is a small piece of data that is _______

options.a: a) sent from a website and stored in user’s web browser while a user is browsing a website
options.b: b) sent from user and stored in the server while a user is browsing a website
options.c: c) sent from root server to all servers
options.d: d) sent from the root server to other root servers

mcqs.answer: a) sent from a website and stored in user’s web browser while a user is browsing a website
mcqs.explanation: A web cookie is a small piece of data sent from a website and stored in user’s web browser while a user is browsing the website and is used to remember stateful information about the user’s operations on the website. This can help the website provide a better browsing experience to the user.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not used to generate dynamic web pages?
mcqs.explanation: CSS alone cannot be used to generate dynamic web pages as it does not provide many event handling functions. It can be used along with JavaScript to generate dynamic web pages which are visually compelling.

mcqs.question: An alternative to JavaScript on windows platform is _______
mcqs.explanation: VBScript is a general-purpose, lightweight and active scripting language which can be used on Microsoft Visual Basic. It was first released in 1996.

mcqs.question: What is document object model (DOM)?

options.a: a) convention for representing and interacting with objects in html documents
options.c: c) hierarchy of objects in ASP.NET

mcqs.answer: a) convention for representing and interacting with objects in html documents
mcqs.explanation: DOM is a hierarchical model i.e. a tree used to represent an HTML or XML document. Every node of the tree an object that represents a part of the document.

mcqs.question: AJAX stands for _______
mcqs.explanation: AJAX is a group of technologies that works on the client-side to create asynchronous web applications. It is used to modify only a part of a webpage and not the whole webpage whenever some event occurs.

links.context:
This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “IPv4”.

Foundational Reading for this Topic: TCP/IP Model

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not applicable for IP?
mcqs.explanation: The Internet Protocol is the networking protocol which establishes the internet by relaying datagrams across network boundaries. ICMP is a supporting protocol for IP which handles the Error Reporting functionality.

mcqs.question: Which of the following field in IPv4 datagram is not related to fragmentation?
mcqs.explanation: TOS-type of service identifies the type of packets. It is not related to fragmentation but is used to request specific treatment such as high throughput, high reliability or low latency for the IP packet depending upon the type of service it belongs to.

mcqs.question: The TTL field has value 10. How many routers (max) can process this datagram?
mcqs.explanation: TTL stands for Time to Live. This field specifies the life of the IP packet based on the number of hops it makes (Number of routers it goes through). TTL field is decremented by one each time the datagram is processed by a router. When the value is 0, the packet is automatically destroyed.

mcqs.question: If the value in protocol field is 17, the transport layer protocol used is _____________
mcqs.explanation: The protocol field enables the demultiplexing feature so that the IP protocol can be used to carry payloads of more than one protocol type. Its most used values are 17 and 6 for UDP and TCP respectively. ICMP and IGMP are network layer protocols.

mcqs.question: The data field cannot carry which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: Data field usually has transport layer segments, but it can also carry ICMP messages. SMTP is an application layer protocol. First it must go through the transport layer to be converted into TCP segments and then it can be inserted into IP packets.

mcqs.question: What should be the flag value to indicate the last fragment?
mcqs.explanation: The Flag field in the IP header is used to control and identify the fragments. It contains three bits: reserved, don’t fragment and more fragments. If the more fragments bit is 0, it means that the fragment is the last fragment.

mcqs.question: Which of these is not applicable for IP protocol?

options.d: d) does not offer error reporting

mcqs.explanation: IP does not provide reliable delivery service for the data. It’s dependent upon the transport layer protocols like TCP to offer reliability.

mcqs.question: Which of the following demerits does Fragmentation have?
mcqs.explanation: Fragmentation makes the implementation of the IP protocol complex and can also be exploited by attackers to create a DOS attack such as a teardrop attack. Fragmentation won’t be required if the transport layer protocols perform wise segmentation.

mcqs.question: Which field helps to check rearrangement of the fragments?
mcqs.explanation: The Fragment Offset field specifies where the fragment fits in the original datagram. The offset of the first fragment will always be 0. The size of the field (13 bits) is 3-bits shorter than the size of the total length field (16 bits).

links.context:
This set of Computer Networks Questions and Answers for Experienced people focuses on “IPv4 Addressing”.

Prep Material for this Topic: Addressing Modes in TCP/IP Model

mcqs.question: Which of these is not applicable for IP protocol?

options.d: d) Does not offer error reporting

mcqs.explanation: IP does not provide reliable delivery service for the data. It’s dependent upon the transport layer protocols like TCP to offer reliability.

mcqs.question: Which of the following demerits does Fragmentation have?
mcqs.explanation: Fragmentation makes the implementation of the IP protocol complex and can also be exploited by attackers to create a DOS attack such as a teardrop attack. Fragmentation won’t be required if the transport layer protocols perform wise segmentation.

mcqs.question: Which field helps to check rearrangement of the fragments?
mcqs.explanation: The Fragment Offset field specifies where the fragment fits in the original datagram. The offset of the first fragment will always be 0. The size of the field (13 bits) is 3-bits shorter than the size of the total length field (16 bits).

mcqs.question: In classless addressing, there are no classes but addresses are still granted in ______
mcqs.explanation: In classless addressing, there are no classes but addresses are still granted in blocks. The total number of addresses in a block of classless IP addresses = 2<sup>(32 – CIDR_value)</sup>.

mcqs.question: In IPv4 Addresses, classful addressing is replaced with ________
mcqs.explanation: Classful addressing is replaced with classless addressing as a large ratio of the available addresses in a class in calssful addressing is wasted. In classless addressing, one can reserve the number of IP addresses required by modifying the CIDR value and make sure that not many addresses are wasted.

mcqs.question: First address in a block is used as network address that represents the ________
mcqs.explanation: First address in a block is used as network address that represents the organization. The network address can be found by AND’ing any address in the block by the default mask. The last address in a block represents the broadcast address.

mcqs.question: In classful addressing, a large part of available addresses are ________
mcqs.explanation: In classful addressing, a large part of available addresses are wasted. Thus to solve this classful addressing is replaced with classless addressing where one can reserve the number of IP addresses required by modifying the CIDR value and make sure that not many addresses are wasted.

mcqs.question: Network addresses are a very important concept of ________
mcqs.explanation: Network addresses are a very important concept of IP addressing. The first address in a block is used as network address that represents the organization. The network address can be found by AND’ing any address in the block or class by the default mask.

mcqs.question: Which of this is not a class of IP address?
mcqs.explanation: Class F is not a class of IP addressing. There are only five classes of IP addresses: Class A (0.0.0.0 to 127.255.255.255), Class B (128.0.0.0 to 191.255.255.255), Class C (192.0.0.0 to 223.255.255.255), Class D (224.0.0.0 to 239.255.255.255), and Class E (240.0.0.0 to 255.255.255.255).

links.context:
This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “IPv6”.

Foundational Reading for this Topic: Internet Protocol (IP)

mcqs.question: The size of an IP address in IPv6 is _________
mcqs.explanation: An IPv6 address is 128 bits long. Therefore, 2128 i.e. 340 undecillion addresses are possible in IPv6. IPv4 has only 4 billion possible addresses and IPv6 would be a brilliant alternative in case IPv4 runs out of possible new addresses.

mcqs.question: The header length of an IPv6 datagram is ___________
mcqs.explanation: IPv6 datagram has fixed header length of 40bytes, which results in faster processing of the datagram. There is one fixed header and optional headers which may or may not exist. The fixed header contains the mandatory essential information about the packet while the optional headers contain the optional “not that necessary” information.

mcqs.question: In the IPv6 header, the traffic class field is similar to which field in the IPv4 header?
mcqs.explanation: The traffic class field is used to specify the priority of the IP packet which is a similar functionality to the Type of Service field in the IPv4 header. It’s an 8-bit field and its values are not defined in the RFC 2460.

mcqs.question: IPv6 does not use _________ type of address.
mcqs.explanation: There is no concept of broadcast address in IPv6. Instead, there is an anycast address in IPv6 which allows sending messages to a group of devices but not all devices in a network. Anycast address is not standardized in IPv4.

mcqs.question: Which among the following features is present in IPv6 but not in IPv4?
mcqs.explanation: There is an anycast address in IPv6 which allows sending messages to a group of devices but not all devices in a network. Anycast address is not standardized in IPv4.

mcqs.question: The _________ field determines the lifetime of IPv6 datagram
mcqs.explanation: The Hop limit value is decremented by one by a router when the datagram is forwarded by the router. When the value becomes zero the datagram is discarded. The field is 8-bits wide, so an IPv6 packet can live up to 255 router hops only.

mcqs.question: Dual-stack approach refers to _________

options.c: c) node has both IPv4 and IPv6 support
options.d: d) implementing a MAC address with 2 stacks

mcqs.answer: c) node has both IPv4 and IPv6 support
mcqs.explanation: Dual-stack is one of the approaches used to support IPv6 in already existing systems. ISPs are using it as a method to transfer from IPv4 to IPv6 completely eventually due to the lower number of possible available addresses in IPv4.

mcqs.question: Suppose two IPv6 nodes want to interoperate using IPv6 datagrams, but they are connected to each other by intervening IPv4 routers. The best solution here is ________
mcqs.explanation: The IPv4 routers can form a tunnel in which at the sender’s side, the IPv6 datagram is encapsulated in to IPv4, and at the receiver’s side of the tunnel, the IPv4 packet is stripped and the IPv6 packet is sent to the receiver.

mcqs.question: Teredo is an automatic tunneling technique. In each client the obfuscated IPv4 address is represented by bits ______
mcqs.explanation: Teredo is a technique through which gives the possibility for full IPv6 network connectivity to IPv6 capable hosts which are currently on an IPv4 network. Bits 96 to 127 in the datagram represents obfuscated 1Pv4 address of the IPv4 network.

links.context:
This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “IPv6 Addressing”.

Prep Material for this Topic: Addressing Modes in TCP/IP Model

mcqs.question: Dual-stack approach refers to _________

options.c: c) Node has both IPv4 and IPv6 support
options.d: d) Implementing a MAC address with 2 stacks

mcqs.answer: c) Node has both IPv4 and IPv6 support
mcqs.explanation: Dual-stack is one of the approaches used to support IPv6 in already existing systems. ISPs are using it as a method to transfer from IPv4 to IPv6 completely eventually due to the lower number of possible available addresses in IPv4.

mcqs.question: Suppose two IPv6 nodes want to interoperate using IPv6 datagrams, but they are connected to each other by intervening IPv4 routers. The best solution here is ________
mcqs.explanation: The IPv4 routers can form a tunnel in which at the sender’s side, the IPv6 datagram is encapsulated in to IPv4, and at the receiver’s side of the tunnel, the IPv4 packet is stripped and the IPv6 packet is sent to the receiver.

mcqs.question: Teredo is an automatic tunneling technique. In each client the obfuscated IPv4 address is represented by bits ______
mcqs.explanation: Teredo is a technique through which gives the possibility for full IPv6 network connectivity to IPv6 capable hosts which are currently on an IPv4 network. Bits 96 to 127 in the datagram represents obfuscated 1Pv4 address of the IPv4 network.

mcqs.question: A link local address of local addresses is used in an _______
mcqs.explanation: Isolated subnet is very huge sharing network area in this link local address of local addresses is used. A link local address can be configured on any subnet with the prefix “FE80::”.

mcqs.question: In subcategories of reserved address in IPv6, address that is used by a host to test itself without going into network is called _________
mcqs.explanation: In subcategories of reserved address in IPv6, address that is used by a host to test itself without going into network is called loop back address. IPv6 loopback address is 0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0001. IPv4 loopback address is 127.0.0.1. It’s a reserved address.

mcqs.question: A few leftmost bits in each address of IPv6 address define its category is called ________
mcqs.explanation: Prefix is the bits in the IP address which are placed in leftmost position. A network prefix in IPv6 is given by a CIDR format-liked number at the end of the address.

mcqs.question: In IPv6 addresses, addresses that start with eight 0s are called ________
mcqs.explanation: In IPv6 address format, the starting bits are specified with eight 0s to represent reserved addresses. These reserved addresses have a certain function pre-defined like the loop-back address is used to test a network card. Reserved addresses cannot be allotted to a machine.

mcqs.question: Which statement(s) about IPv6 addresses are true?

options.b: b) Two colons (::) are used to represent successive hexadecimal fields of zeros
options.c: c) Two colons (::) are used to separate fields
options.d: d) A single interface cannot have multiple IPv6 addresses of different types

mcqs.answer: b) Two colons (::) are used to represent successive hexadecimal fields of zeros
mcqs.explanation: In order to shorten the written length of an IPv6 address, successive fields of zeros may be replaced by double colons. In trying to shorten the address further, leading zeros may also be removed. Just as with IPv4, a single device’s interface can have more than one address; with IPv6 there are more types of addresses and the same rule applies. There can be link-local, global unicast, and multicast addresses all assigned to the same interface.

mcqs.question: When was IPv6 launched?
mcqs.explanation: IPv6 is the latest version of the Internet Protocol released on 6<sup>th</sup> June 2012. An IPv6 address is 128 bits long. Therefore, 2<sup>128</sup> i.e. 340 undecillion addresses are possible in IPv6.

links.context: This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “P2P Applications”.

mcqs.question: Which layer is responsible for process-to-process delivery?
mcqs.explanation: The transport layer is responsible for process-to-process delivery, error control and flow control. It provides an interface for the implementation of process to process delivery through ports. There are 65,535 port numbers.

mcqs.question: In process-to-process delivery, two processes communicate in which of the following methods?
mcqs.explanation: The most common method used for this communication is Client/Server. The client requests a service through a particular port number to the port of the server using its socket address. Then the server responds by giving the requested service to the client port.

mcqs.question: Multiple processes on destinations at transport layer are identified by __________
mcqs.explanation: Multiple processes on destinations are identified by a transport layer address also called as port number. The IP address along with the port number is called the socket address.

mcqs.question: Range of port numbers in Internet model is __________
mcqs.explanation: Port numbers are 16-bit integers between 0 and 65,535. They are an interface for the implementation of process to process delivery for the transport layer.

mcqs.question: According to Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA), which of the following ranges is not a part of port number ranges?
mcqs.explanation: IANA divided port numbers into three ranges i.e., Well-known, Registered and Dynamic ports. Well-known port numbers range from 0 to 1023, registered port numbers are from 1024 to 49151 and dynamic port numbers are from 49152 to 65535.

mcqs.question: The combination of an IP address and port number is called as ________
mcqs.explanation: Socket address is the combination of an IP address and a port number and it is used to define the client-end and server-end processes uniquely.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is false with respect to Connectionless service of transport layer protocol?

options.d: d) Packet may arrive out of sequence

mcqs.explanation: There is a high probability in connectionless services like UDP that the packet gets delayed or lost because there is no connection made between the two end nodes. No connection means that there is no unique pathway for the packets to travel.

mcqs.question:
Correct order in the process of Connection-Oriented services is ________ i. Data transfer
ii. Connection release
iii. Connection establishment
mcqs.explanation: First the client has to request a connection and the server has to accept the connection to establish a connection. Then data transfer can start between the two ends. Then both client and server need to terminate their ends to terminate the connection.

mcqs.question: In transport layer, Multiplexing is done at _________
mcqs.explanation: At the sender’s side, there are multiple processes which may want to send packets. But there is only one transport layer protocol like TCP or UDP working at a time. So the transport layer protocol gets the messages from these processes and separates them with different port numbers. This process is called multiplexing and it is done before sending packets to the receivers side.

mcqs.question: The process of error checking and dropping of the header, delivering messages to appropriate process based on port number is called as _______
mcqs.explanation: Demultiplexing is the process of error checking and dropping of the header, delivering messages to appropriate process based on port number. The transport layer does this on the receiver’s end after the packet is received and takes help of the header attached by the sender’s side transport layer during multiplexing.

links.context: This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “ICMP”.

mcqs.question: Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) has been designed to compensate _________
mcqs.explanation: IP by itself does not provide the features of error reporting or error correction. So, to address these issues a network layer protocol called Internet Control Message Protocol is used. ICMP operates over the IP packet to provide error reporting functionality.

mcqs.question: Header size of the ICMP message is _________
mcqs.explanation: An ICMP message has an 8-byte header and a variable size data section. Out of the 8 bytes, the first 4 bytes are of a fixed format having the type, code and checksum fields and the next 4 bytes depend upon the type of the message.

mcqs.question: During error reporting, ICMP always reports error messages to ________
mcqs.explanation: ICMP notifies the source about the error when an error is detected because the datagram knows information about source and destination IP address. The source can then retransmit the data again or try to correct those errors.

mcqs.question: Which of these is not a type of error-reporting message?
mcqs.explanation: Router error is not a type of error-reporting message in ICMP. The type of error reporting message is specified in the ICMP header. Destination unreachable is type 3 error message, source quench is type 4, and time exceeded is type 11 error message.

mcqs.question: ICMP error message will not be generated for a datagram having a special address such as _______
mcqs.explanation: 127.0.0.0 is a special address known as the loopback address which is used for testing purpose of a machine without actually communicating with a network. Thus no error reporting message will be generated for such special addresses.

mcqs.question: When a router cannot route a datagram or host cannot deliver a datagram, the datagram is discarded and the router or the host sends a ____________ message back to the source host that initiated the datagram.
mcqs.explanation: Router sends destination unreachable message if the destination is not found. Destination unreachable is type 3 error reporting message. It is invoked when the router can’t find a path to the intended destination to forward the packet through.

mcqs.question: The source-quench message in ICMP was designed to add a kind of ____________ to the IP.
mcqs.explanation: Firstly, it informs the source that the datagram has been discarded. Secondly, it warns the source that there is congestion in the network. It’s type 4 error reporting message after which the source is expected to reduce the flow of packets.

mcqs.question: In case of time exceeded error, when the datagram visits a router, the value of time to live field is _________
mcqs.explanation: This field will be decremented by 1 at every router, and will be zero by the time it reaches source. This error reporting message is type 11 and is used to prevent the router from travelling forever in case some unknown path anomaly occurs.

mcqs.question: Two machines can use the timestamp request and timestamp replay messages to determine the ___________ needed for an IP datagram to travel between them.

options.c: c) Travel time for the next router
options.d: d) Time to reach the destination/source

mcqs.explanation: The round-trip time refers to the total time taken combining the time taken for a packet sent from a source to reach a destination and the time taken the acknowledgement sent by the destination to reach the source. The Router sends destination unreachable message if the destination is not found.

mcqs.question: During debugging, we can use the ____________ program to find if a host is alive and responding.
mcqs.explanation: Ping program is used to find if a host is alive and responding. It is to be entered into a command line with the syntax “ping (IP address)” to be executed. Traceroute is a program used to find the shortest route to the destination IP.

mcqs.question: In windows  ____________ can be used to trace the route of the packet from the source to the destination.
mcqs.explanation: Tracert is used in case of windows, whereas Traceroute in UNIX. Tracert is a program used to find the shortest route to the destination IP. The Router sends destination unreachable message if a path to the destination IP is not found.

mcqs.question: In a simple echo-request message, the value of the sum is 01010000 01011100. Then, value of checksum is ___________
mcqs.explanation: The sender side adds the bits of the fragmented packet to find a sum. Checksum is the compliment of the sum (exchange 0’s and 1’s). The receiver then has to verify the checksum by adding the bits of the received packet to ensure that the packet is error-free.

links.context: This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Mail Access Protocols”.

mcqs.question: Which mail access protocol is used for sending emails across the internet?
mcqs.explanation: SMTP is the standard protocol for sending emails across the internet whereas POP3 and IMAP are standard protocols for retrieving emails. MAPI is an interface that helps programs become email aware.

mcqs.question: POP3 is used to access emails from multiple clients/computers.
mcqs.explanation: POP3 is used to access email from only one client. IMAP is used to simultaneously access email from multiple clients.

mcqs.question: Which of the following port is used by clients to connect using IMAP securely?
mcqs.explanation: Port 993 is used by clients to connect using IMAP securely. Port 80 is used by the HTTP protocol, Port 143 is used for non-encrypted IMAP connection and Port 2525 is used by the SMTP protocol.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the default POP3 port number?
mcqs.explanation: Port 110 is the default port for non-encrypted POP3. Port 995 is used for secure connection using POP3, Port 2525 is used by SMTP for non-encrypted connection and Port 143 is used for non-encrypted connection by IMAP.

mcqs.question: The default port number of SMTP is _________
mcqs.explanation: The default port number for SMTP is 25. Port 110 and Port 143 are the default port numbers for POP3 and IMAP respectively. Port number 2525 is used by SMTP when port number 25 is filtered out and the client wishes for a non-encrypted connection.

mcqs.question: POP3 protocol belongs to which layer of the ISO OSI model?
mcqs.explanation: POP3 protocol is an application layer protocol used by email clients to retrieve emails. Protocols like MAC, IP, and TCP, work on the Data Link layer, Network layer, and Transport layer respectively.

mcqs.question: Which mail access protocol is used for accessing email from multiple clients?
mcqs.explanation: IMAP protocol is used when an email is to be accessed from multiple clients. POP3 is used to provide email access to a single program or client whereas SMTP is used for sending emails. SNMP is used for managing devices on the network.

mcqs.question: Which port is used for sending messages using SMTP securely?
mcqs.explanation: Port number 465 is used for sending messages using SMTP securely. Port 110 and Port 995 are used by POP3 and Port 143 is the default port number for IMAP.

mcqs.question: Which protocol forbids users from making any modifications like create, delete or rename emails on the mail server?
mcqs.explanation: POP3 forbids users from making any modifications to the emails on the email server to ensure that no emails are corrupted. IMAP allows such modifications as it can keep up with the modifications. SMTP and MAPI are used for sending emails and providing an interface for programs to make them email aware respectively.

mcqs.question: IMAP protocol is used to ___________

options.a: a) To manage devices on the network
options.b: b) Sending an email through the internet
options.c: c) Download the entire email account inbox on the computer
options.d: d) Synchronizes email on the computer with the email account’s email-server

mcqs.answer: d) Synchronizes email on the computer with the email account’s email-server
mcqs.explanation: IMAP protocol is used to synchronize email on the computer with the email account’s email-server. SNMP is used for managing network devices, SMTP is used for sending email through the internet, and POP3 is used to download the entire email account inbox on the computer.

links.context: This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Transition from IPV4 to IPV6”.

mcqs.question: The main reason for transition from IPv4 to IPv6 is _________

options.a: a) Huge number of systems on the internet
options.b: b) Very low number of system on the internet

mcqs.answer: a) Huge number of systems on the internet
mcqs.explanation: Due to huge number of systems on the internet and the lower number of available addresses on IPv4, transition from IPv4 to IPv6 needs to happen. IPv4 provides around 4 billion unique IP addresses whereas IPv6 provides over 340 undecillion unique IP addresses.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a transition strategy?
mcqs.explanation: As IPv4 addresses are of 32 bits and IPv6 addresses are of 128 bits, it is not possible to convert IPv4 address to IPv6 address. So, Dual stack, tunneling and header translation are the three strategies which might help in the transition from IPv4 to IPv6.

mcqs.question: To determine which version to use when sending a packet to a destination, the source host queries which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: Source host queries DNS to determine which version to use when sending a packet to a destination. The DNS contains both, the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses of the modern dual stack host servers.

mcqs.question: The strategy used when two computers using IPv6 want to communicate with each other and the packet must pass through a region that uses IPv4 is ______________
mcqs.explanation: In tunneling, The IPv4 routers can form a tunnel in which at the sender’s side, the IPv6 datagram is encapsulated in to IPv4, and at the receiver’s side of the tunnel, the IPv4 packet is stripped and the IPv6 packet is sent to the receiver.

mcqs.question:
The correct format of packet in tunnel that uses IPv4 region is ________ i. IPv6 header
ii. Payload
iii. IPv4 header
mcqs.explanation: At the sender’s side, the IPv6 datagram is encapsulated in to IPv4 i.e. An IPv4 header is inserted on top of the IPv6 header, and then the packet is sent through the tunnel.

mcqs.question: ___________ is necessary when the sender wants to use IPv6, but the receiver does not understand IPv6.
mcqs.explanation: Header translation is used when the sender wants to use IPv6, but the receiver does not understand IPv6. It is made possible through a Network Address Translation – Protocol Translation enabled device such as a gateway.

mcqs.question: Header translation uses ___________ to translate an IPv6 address to an IPv4 address.
mcqs.explanation: A mapped IPv6 address contains the IPv4 address in its last 32-bits and is preceded by 16 1s and 80 0s. It can be used to translate an IPv6 address to an IPv4 address.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a step in the Header translation procedure?

options.a: a) The IPv6 mapped address is changed to an IPv4 address by extracting the rightmost 32bits
options.b: b) The value of the IPv6 priority field is discarded
options.c: c) The type of service field in IPv4 is set to zero
options.d: d) The IPv6 flow label is considered

mcqs.answer: d) The IPv6 flow label is considered
mcqs.explanation: In the header translation procedure, first the IPv6 mapped address is changed to an IPv4 address by extracting the rightmost 32bits, then the value of the IPv6 priority field is discarded, and finally the ToS field in the IPv4 header is set to zero. IPv6 flow label is ignored in the procedure.

links.context:
This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “IPV4 and IPV6 Comparision”.

Foundational Reading for this Topic: Internet Protocol (IP)

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not applicable for IP?
mcqs.explanation: The Internet Protocol is the networking protocol that establishes the internet by relaying datagram across network boundaries. ICMP is a supporting protocol for IP which handles the Error Reporting functionality.

mcqs.question: Which of the following field in IPv4 datagram is not related to fragmentation?
mcqs.explanation: TOS-type of service identifies the type of packets. It is not related to fragmentation but is used to request specific treatment such as high throughput, high reliability or low latency for the IP packet depending upon the type of service it belongs to.

mcqs.question: The TTL field has value 10. How many routers (max) can process this datagram?
mcqs.explanation: TTL stands for Time to Live. This field specifies the life of the IP packet based on the number of hops it makes (Number of routers it goes through). TTL field is decremented by one each time the datagram is processed by a router. When the value is 0, the packet is automatically destroyed.

mcqs.question: If the value in protocol field is 17, the transport layer protocol used is _________
mcqs.explanation: The protocol field enables the demultiplexing feature so that the IP protocol can be used to carry payloads of more than one protocol type. Its most used values are 17 and 6 for UDP and TCP respectively. ICMP and IGMP are network layer protocols.

mcqs.question: Which field helps to check rearrangement of the fragments?
mcqs.explanation: The Fragment Offset field specifies where the fragment fits in the original datagram. The offset of the first fragment will always be 0. The size of the field (13 bits) is 3-bits shorter than the size of the total length field (16 bits).

mcqs.question: The size of an IP address in IPv6 is _________
mcqs.explanation: An IPv6 address is 128 bits long. Therefore, 2<sup>128</sup> i.e. 340 undecillion unique addresses are available in IPv6. IPv4 has only 4 billion possible addresses and IPv6 would be a brilliant alternative in case IPv4 runs out of possible new addresses.

mcqs.question: The header length of an IPv6 datagram is ___________
mcqs.explanation: IPv6 datagram has fixed header length of 40bytes, which results in faster processing of the datagram. There is one fixed header and optional headers which may or may not exist. The fixed header contains the mandatory essential information about the packet while the optional headers contain the optional “not that necessary” information.

mcqs.question: In an IPv6 header, the traffic class field is similar to which field in the IPv4 header?
mcqs.explanation: The traffic class field is used to specify the priority of the IP packet which is a similar functionality to the Type of Service field in the IPv4 header. It’s an 8-bit field and its values are not defined in the RFC 2460.

mcqs.question: IPv6 does not use ________ type of address.
mcqs.explanation: There is no concept of broadcast address in IPv6. Instead, there is an anycast address in IPv6 which allows sending messages to a group of devices but not all devices in a network. Anycast address is not standardized in IPv4.

links.context:
This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Routers and its Functionalities Basics”.

Technical Primer for this Topic: Network Devices Overview

mcqs.question: In virtual circuit, each packet is routed independently.
mcqs.explanation: Every host will be setting a predefined path if the host wants to send packets through virtual circuit network, and all the packets should abide by the same path. Each packet will have a virtual circuit identifier along with the data.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is correct according to the definition of routing algorithm?

options.a: a) It takes care of the routing tables
options.b: b) It is responsible for routing decisions
options.c: c) It is responsible for routing decisions but does not manage tables
options.d: d) It manages the routing tables and responsible for routing decisions

mcqs.answer: d) It manages the routing tables and responsible for routing decisions
mcqs.explanation: Routing algorithms manage the routing tables according to the traffic in the network and make changes in them. Router makes routing decisions using routing algorithm. The routing algorithms make use of current routing information and are used to make decisions.

mcqs.question: Which address is used by the router to forward packets?
mcqs.explanation: IP address is used by the routers to send packets from source to destination. Each packet has a unique IP address of the destination host. Routers make use of these unique numbers to forward the packets to the correct destination. Remaining addresses are used at different layers.

mcqs.question: What message will be returned by the router if it receives data more than its capacity?
mcqs.explanation: Source quench is an ICMP message. It is used by the router or destination host when they receive data at a rate that they can not handle. Upon receiving the message, the source host should decrease the load until it no longer receives the same message.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is incorrect about routers?

options.a: a) Router is a network layer device
options.b: b) A Router can be used to transmit the packets across the networks
options.c: c) Routers do not have memory
options.d: d) Routers work in half and full duplex mode

mcqs.answer: c) Routers do not have memory
mcqs.explanation: Routers do have memory. Routers use memory just like any computer for processing. And also routers use memory for storing the routing tables. A router can connect networks which are similar.

mcqs.question: Which address is obtained in return if a router sends an ARP query packet?

options.a: a) Physical address of the receiver
options.b: b) IP address of the  sender
options.c: c) Physical address of the sender
options.d: d) IP address of the receiver

mcqs.answer: a) Physical address of the receiver
mcqs.explanation: An ARP query packet contains both the physical address and logical address of the sender(router) and logical address of the receiver. This packet is used to acquire the physical address of the destination host. This physical address of the receiver helps the datagram to pass through physical network.

mcqs.question: Which of the following can be used by a router to increase the processing speed of the packet?
mcqs.explanation: A router can contain a flow label table if it is capable of supporting flow labels. Flow label helps the router to find the next hop without consulting the routing table. If the router does not supports the flow label then it simply leaves it aside.

mcqs.question: Router belongs to which layer?
mcqs.explanation: Router belongs to network layer in OSI architecture. Routers are mainly used for packet switching between networks. Bridge and switch are data link layer devices. Repeater and hub are physical layer devices. Application gateway is used in application layer.

mcqs.question: In which routing, the destination address field contains the address of the next router?
mcqs.explanation: Generally, the field of destination address contains the final destination address of the packet, but in the source routing the address field is filled by the address of the router which is going to be visited next.

mcqs.question: Congestion avoidance is difficult in datagram network than virtual circuit.
mcqs.explanation: It is true that congestion avoidance is difficult in datagram network. These networks do not reserve the resources in advance and also the router’s capacity can not be known before transmission. These reasons cause the congestion difficult to avoid in datagram network.

links.context:
This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “LS Routing Algorithms”.

Technical Prep Guide for this Topic: Distance Vector vs Link State Routing

mcqs.question: Which routing algorithm was replaced by link state routing algorithm in the ARPANET?
mcqs.explanation: Originally, the ARPANET used distance vector routing in it but later it was replaced by link state routing. This is because of the count-to-infinity problem in distance vector routing. Unlike DVR, routing tables in LS routing contain whole topology of the network.

mcqs.question: Same topology is used by all the nodes to construct a routing table in link state routing.
mcqs.explanation: In link state routing, the routing tables are different but the topology they perceive is same. Because of this same topology, each node will have a shortest path for every node in the network.

mcqs.question: What is flooding in link state routing in case of exchanging topology information?

options.a: a) Exposing routing tables to neighbors
options.b: b) Sending duplicate packets to nodes
options.c: c) Communicating with every router using messages

mcqs.explanation: Link state packets are used to spread the information about the topology from one node to all nodes. It can be periodic or triggered and it carries information about both topology and itself to other nodes.

mcqs.question: Which information in the link state packets helps in discarding old link state packets?

options.d: d) Number of nodes it visits

mcqs.explanation: Every link state packet, which is created by a node will have the data about its age. This age information is used to dispose the old packets from the domain which are timed out.

mcqs.question: Which sequence of procedure is correct to build a routing table in link state routing?

options.a: a) Creating LSP – flooding – shortest path tree – calculating routing table
options.b: b) Shortest path tree – flooding – creating LSP – calculating routing table
options.c: c) Creating LSP – flooding – calculating routing table – shortest path tree
options.d: d) Shortest path tree – flooding – calculating routing table -creating LSP

mcqs.answer: a) Creating LSP – flooding – shortest path tree – calculating routing table
mcqs.explanation: Once all nodes get familiar with the topology using flooding, which is done using LSP, then a shortest path tree will be constructed for each node. Shortest path trees are used to calculate the routing tables and each router will have one shortest path tree.

mcqs.question: Which algorithm is used by the router in the link state routing to find the shortest paths?
mcqs.explanation: Shortest path trees will be constructed to build the routing tables and router uses Dijkstra algorithm to compute the routes. Dijkstra algorithm finds the shortest route for every destination in the network for a router and this information will be memorized.

mcqs.question: Which algorithm is implemented based on link state routing?
mcqs.explanation: Open shortest path first(OSPF) is based on link state routing which works in an autonomous domain and it is a dynamic routing protocol. This protocol works well by dividing the autonomous system into areas.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an advantage of the link state routing?
mcqs.explanation: Link state routing causes less loops when compared to distance vector routing. It is because, complete topology information will be there at each router and this information prevents misunderstandings which leads to loops.

mcqs.question: What is the full form of  LSA in link state routing, which is used to exchange information between routers?
mcqs.explanation: Routers share the information about topology using link state advertisements. There will be a continuous process of passing these link state advertisements until every router get the full topology of the network.

mcqs.question: Link state routing is confined to inter-domain routing.
mcqs.explanation: Link state routing can be used within the autonomous system only, because flooding is unmanageable in a large network. Because, network is a collection of such autonomous systems.

links.context:
This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “DV Routing Algorithms”.

Technical Prep Guide for this Topic: Distance Vector vs Link State Routing

mcqs.question: What is the other name for distance vector routing algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: DVR is a dynamic and intra-domain routing protocol which is developed by Bellman and ford. It is the evolved version of the original ARPANET and it is more efficient than flooding.

mcqs.question: How tables are updated in the distance vector routing algorithm?

options.b: b) By retrieving the information from all the nodes directly
options.c: c) By interchanging the information with neighbour nodes
options.d: d) By exchanging the information with a central device

mcqs.answer: c) By interchanging the information with neighbour nodes
mcqs.explanation: In distance vector routing algorithm, routing tables exchange their information only with their neighbour nodes. So, gradually tables will be updated with least distance routes for each destination and it will have information about next hop for each route.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a similarity between flooding and distance vector routing?
mcqs.explanation: Both flooding technique and distance vector routing are used to find shortest paths for the destinations. But flooding requires less setup than DVR because, nodes in it need to know information about their neighbors only. And it needs less memory with less setup.

mcqs.question: Which statement is correct about routing tables in distance vector routing?

options.a: a) Routing tables have entry for only immediate neighbouring nodes
options.b: b) Routing tables have entry for all the nodes in the network
options.c: c) Routing tables have entry for those nodes who have minimum distance
options.d: d) Routing tables have entry for those nodes who have maximum distance

mcqs.answer: b) Routing tables have entry for all the nodes in the network
mcqs.explanation: In distance vector routing, routing tables have single entry for each node which is present in the network. But each router exchanges the information with neighboring nodes only.

mcqs.question: What is the default distance between two nodes in the initial routing table, if these two nodes are not immediate neighbors in distance vector routing?

options.a: a) Maximum distance in the routing table of the node
options.b: b) Minimum distance in the routing table of the node
options.c: c) Infinite distance that is unreachable
options.d: d) Total sum of the distances in the routing table

mcqs.answer: c) Infinite distance that is unreachable
mcqs.explanation: In DVR, if nodes are neighbors, they can send messages to find distance between them. But if the nodes are not neighbors then the distance between them is infinite initially. Later this infinity will be replaced with distance by the router.

mcqs.question: What update can it be called, if a node sends its routing table to its neighbors if there are any modifications in the routing table?
mcqs.explanation: Triggered update may happen when there is change in the routing table of the node or failure of neighboring links. It can happen at any time if a node is subjected to changes.

mcqs.question: Which protocols are considered as intra-domain routing protocols?

options.a: a) Distance vector and link state routing
options.b: b) Distance vector and path vector routing
options.c: c) Path vector and link state routing
options.d: d) Only a path vector routing

mcqs.answer: a) Distance vector and link state routing
mcqs.explanation: Distance vector routing and link state routing are used with in an autonomous system and cannot work well in between autonomous systems. Scalability differs between intra-domain and inter-domain routing protocols.

mcqs.question: Which technique can be used in multicast routing to overcome the problem of count-to-infinity which occurs in distance vector routing?
mcqs.explanation: Basically, flooding in distance vector routing causes the loops in multicast routing. In order to overcome this problem, reverse path forwarding does not allow the router to send the packets to the link that on which it has received the packet.

mcqs.question: Which routing does not permit the router to send its routing table to its neighboring nodes?
mcqs.explanation: Multicast distance vector routing uses the multicast routing technique and source based trees. Router uses its own uni-cast routing table and evanescent shortest path trees for forwarding packets instead of exchanging routing table for information.

mcqs.question: Distance vector routing is a dynamic routing algorithm.
mcqs.explanation: Distance vector routing uses dynamic routing tables and these routing tables make use of dynamic routing protocols. The routing tables update themselves dynamically, according to the changes in the inter network.

links.context: This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Analyzing Subnet Masks”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the broadcast address for a Class B network ID using the default subnetmask?
mcqs.explanation: In this case, the class B network ID is 172.16.0.0. We know that the default mask of a class B network is 255.255.0.0. If we OR any address in a network with the complement of the default mask (0.0.255.255), we get the broadcast address of the network. In this case, the result of OR would be 172.16.255.255.

mcqs.question: You have an IP address of 172.16.13.5 with a 255.255.255.128 subnet mask. What is your class of address, subnet address, and broadcast address?

options.a: a) Class A, Subnet 172.16.13.0, Broadcast address 172.16.13.127
options.b: b) Class B, Subnet 172.16.13.0, Broadcast address 172.16.13.127
options.c: c) Class B, Subnet 172.16.13.0, Broadcast address 172.16.13.255
options.d: d) Class B, Subnet 172.16.0.0, Broadcast address 172.16.255.255

mcqs.answer: b) Class B, Subnet 172.16.13.0, Broadcast address 172.16.13.127
mcqs.explanation: We know that the prefix 172 lies in class B (128 to 191) of IPv4 addresses. From the subnet mask, we get that the class is divided into 2 subnets: 172.16.13.0 to 172.16.13.127 and 172.16.13.128 to 172.16.13.255. The IP 172.16.13.5 lies in the first subnet. So the starting address 172.16.13.0 is the subnet address and last address 172.16.13.127 is the broadcast address.

mcqs.question: If you wanted to have 12 subnets with a Class C network ID, which subnet mask would you use?
mcqs.explanation:
If you have eight networks and each requires 10 hosts, you would use the Class C mask of 255.255.255.240. Why? Because 240 in binary is 11110000, which means you have four subnet bits and four host bits. Using our math, we’d get the following:
24-2=14 subnets
24-2=14 hosts.

mcqs.question: The combination of _________ and __________ is often termed the local address of the local portion of the IP address.

options.a: a) Network number and host number
options.b: b) Network number and subnet number
options.c: c) Subnet number and host number

mcqs.answer: c) Subnet number and host number
mcqs.explanation: It is termed as the local address because the address won’t be applicable outside the subnet. Sub networking is implemented for remote sensing in transparent way from that host which is contained in the sub network which called a local operation.

mcqs.question: _________ implies that all subnets obtained from the same subnet mask.
mcqs.explanation: Static subnetting is used when the requirement is of same number of hosts in each subnet for the institution. The same subnet mask can be used to find the subnet id of each subnet. It is usually used to divide large networks into smaller parts.

mcqs.question:
State whether true or false. i) A connection oriented protocol can only use unicast addresses.
ii) The any cast service is included in IPV6.
mcqs.explanation: In a connection oriented protocol, the host can only establish connection with another host on one unique channel, that’s why it can only use unicast addresses. In IPv6, there is an anycast address in IPv6 which allows sending messages to a group of devices but not all devices in a network.

mcqs.question: __________ is a high performance fiber optic token ring LAN running at 100 Mbps over distances upto 1000 stations connected.
mcqs.explanation: FDDI stands for Fiber Distributed Data Interface. It is a set of standards for fiber optic token ring LANs running at 100 Mbps over distances up to 200 km in diameter and 1000 stations connected.

mcqs.question: Which of the following are Gigabit Ethernets?
mcqs.explanation: In computer networking, Gigabit Ethernet (GbE or 1 GigE) is a term describing various technologies for transmitting Ethernet frames at a rate of a gigabit per second (1,000,000,000 bits per second), as defined by the IEEE 802.3-2008 standard. It came into use beginning in 1999, gradually supplanting Fast Ethernet in wired local networks, as a result of being considerably faster.

mcqs.question: _________ is a collective term for a number of Ethernet Standards that carry traffic at the nominal rate of 1000 Mbit/s against the original Ethernet speed of 10 Mbit/s.
mcqs.explanation: Fast Ethernet is a set of Ethernet Standards which were introduced in 1995, that carry traffic at the nominal rate of 1000 Mbit/s. 100BASE-TX is the most commonly used Fast Ethernet standard.

mcqs.question: _________ is another kind of fiber optic network with an active star for switching.
mcqs.explanation: A 50-MBd active star fiber optical Local area network (LAN) and its optical combiner and mixing rod splitter are presented. The limited power budget and relatively large tapping losses of light wave technology, which limit the use of fiber optics in tapped bus LAN topologies, are examined and proven tolerable in optical star topologies.

mcqs.question:
A network administrator is connecting hosts A and B directly through their Ethernet interfaces, as shown in the illustration. Ping attempts between the hosts are unsuccessful. What can be done to provide connectivity between the hosts? 
i. A crossover cable should be used in place of the straight-through cable.
ii. A rollover cable should be used in place of the straight-through cable.
iii. The subnet masks should be set to 255.255.255.192.
iv. A default gateway needs to be set on each host.
v. The subnet masks should be set to 255.255.255.0.
mcqs.explanation: First, if you have two hosts directly connected, as shown in the graphic, then you need a crossover cable. A straight-through cable won’t work. Second, the hosts have different masks, which puts them in different subnets. The easy solution is just to set both masks to 255.255.255.0 (/24).

mcqs.question:
Your router has the following IP address on Ethernet0: 172.16.2.1/23. Which of the following can be valid host IDs on the LAN interface attached to the router? 
i. 172.16.1.100
ii. 172.16.1.198
iii. 172.16.2.255
iv. 172.16.3.0
mcqs.explanation: The router’s IP address on the E0 interface is 172.16.2.1/23, which is 255.255.254.0. This makes the third octet a block size of 2. The router’s interface is in the 172.16.2.0 subnet, and the broadcast address is 172.16.3.255 because the next subnet is 172.16.4.0. The valid host range is 172.16.2.1 to 172.16.3.254. The router is using the first valid host address in the range.

mcqs.question:
Which two statements describe the IP address 10.16.3.65/23? 
i. The subnet address is 10.16.3.0 255.255.254.0.
ii. The lowest host address in the subnet is 10.16.2.1 255.255.254.0.
iii. The last valid host address in the subnet is 10.16.2.254 255.255.254.0.
iv. The broadcast address of the subnet is 10.16.3.255 255.255.254.0.
mcqs.explanation: The mask 255.255.254.0 (/23) used with a Class A address means that there are 15 subnet bits and 9 host bits. The block size in the third octet is 2 (256 – 254). So this makes the subnets in the interesting octet 0, 2, 4, 6, etc., all the way to 254. The host 10.16.3.65 is in the 10.16.2.0 subnet. The next subnet is 10.16.4.0, so the broadcast address for the 10.16.2.0 subnet is 10.16.3.255. The valid host addresses are 10.16.2.1 to 10.16.3.254.

mcqs.question: What is the maximum number of IP addresses that can be assigned to hosts on a local subnet that uses the 255.255.255.224 subnet mask?
mcqs.explanation: A /27 (255.255.255.224) is 3 bits on and 5 bits off. This provides 8 subnets, each with 30 hosts. Does it matter if this mask is used with a Class A, B, or C network address? Not at all. The number of host bits would never change.

mcqs.question: You need to subnet a network into 5 subnets, each with at least 16 hosts. Which classful subnet mask would you use?
mcqs.explanation: You need 5 subnets, each with at least 16 hosts. The mask 255.255.255.240 provides 16 subnets with 14 hosts which is less than 15, so this will not work. The mask 255.255.255.224 provides 8 subnets, each with 30 hosts so this may work. The mask 255.255.255.192 provides 4 subnets, each with 60 hosts so this may work. Comparing both the possible masks, 255.255.255.224 provides the best answer.

mcqs.question: You have a network that needs 29 subnets while maximizing the number of host addresses available on each subnet. How many bits must you borrow from the host field to provide the correct subnet mask?
mcqs.explanation: A 240 mask is 4 subnet bits and provides 16 subnets, each with 14 hosts. We need more subnets, so let’s add subnet bits. One more subnet bit would be a 248 mask. This provides 5 subnet bits (32 subnets) with 3 host bits (6 hosts per subnet). This is the best answer.

mcqs.question: If an Ethernet port on a router were assigned an IP address of 172.16.112.1/25, what would be the valid subnet address of this host?
mcqs.explanation: A /25 mask is 255.255.255.128. Used with a Class B network, the third and fourth octets are used for subnetting with a total of 9 subnet bits, 8 bits in the third octet and 1 bit in the fourth octet. Since there is only 1 bit in the fourth octet, the bit is either off or on-which is a value of 0 or 128. The host in the question is in the 0 subnet, which has a broadcast address of 127 since 128 is the next subnet

mcqs.question: You have an interface on a router with the IP address of 192.168.192.10/29. Including the router interface, how many hosts can have IP addresses on the LAN attached to the router interface?
mcqs.explanation: A /29 (255.255.255.248), regardless of the class of address, has only 3 host bits. Six hosts are the maximum number of hosts on this LAN, including the router interface. Out of the 8 addresses possible with the host bits, the first and the last address are for the subnet id and broadcast address respectively.

mcqs.question: What is the subnet id of a host with an IP address 172.16.66.0/21?
mcqs.explanation: A /21 is 255.255.248.0, which means we have a block size of 8 in the third octet, so we just count by 8 until we reach 66. The subnet in this question is 64.0. The next subnet is 72.0, so the broadcast address of the 64 subnet is 71.255.

mcqs.question: The network address of 172.16.0.0/19 provides how many subnets and hosts?
mcqs.explanation: A CIDR address of /19 is 255.255.224.0. This is a Class B address, so that is only 3 subnet bits, but it provides 13 host bits, or 8 subnets, each with 8,190 hosts.

links.context: This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “IP Routing”.

mcqs.question: Which type of Ethernet framing is used for TCP/IP and DEC net?
mcqs.explanation: The Ethernet 802.3 framing is used for NetWare versions 2 to 3.11, and the Ethernet 802.2 framing is used for NetWare versions 3.12 and later plus OSI routing, Ethernet II is used with TCP/IP and DEC net, and Ethernet SNAP is used with TCP/IP and AppleTalk. The type field in Ethernet 802.2 frame is replaced by a length field in Ethernet 802.3.

mcqs.question: Consider a situation in which you are a system administrator on a NetWare network, you are running NetWare 4.11 and you cannot communicate with your router. What is the likely problem?

options.c: c) Cisco routers only work with NetWare 3.11

mcqs.explanation: The default encapsulation on Cisco routers is Novell Ethernet_802.3 and NetWare 3.12and later defaults to 802.2 encapsulation, 3.11 and earlier defaults to 802.3.

mcqs.question: NetWare IPX addressing uses a network number and a node number. Which statement is not true?

options.a: a) The network address is administratively assigned and can be up to 16 hexadecimal digits long
options.b: b) The node address is always administratively assigned
options.c: c) The node address is usually the MAC address
options.d: d) If the MAC address is used as the node address, then IPX eliminates the use of ARP

mcqs.answer: b) The node address is always administratively assigned
mcqs.explanation: The network address can be up to 16 hexadecimal digits in length. The node number is 12 hexadecimal digits. The node address is usually the MAC address. An example IPX address is 4a1d.0000.0c56.de33. The network part is 4a1d. The node part is 0000.0c56.de33. The network number is assigned by the system administrator of the Novell network and the MAC address/node address is not assigned by the administrator.

mcqs.question: Which NetWare protocol works on layer 3–network layer—of the OSI model?
mcqs.explanation: IPX (Internetwork Packet Exchange) is the NetWare network layer 3 protocol used for transferring information on LANs that use Novell’s NetWare.

mcqs.question: Which NetWare protocol provides link-state routing?
mcqs.explanation: NetWare Link Services Protocol (NLSP) provides link-state routing. SAP (Service Advertisement Protocol) advertises network services. NCP (NetWare Core Protocol) provides client-to-server connections and applications. RIP is a distance vector routing protocol. NLSP was developed by Novell to replace RIP routing protocols.

mcqs.question: As a system administrator, you want to debug IGRP but are worried that the “debug IP IGRP transaction” command will flood the console. What is the command that you should use?
mcqs.explanation: The “debug IP IGRP events” is used to display a short summary of IGRP routing information. You can append an IP address onto either console’s command-line to see only the IGRP updates from a neighbor. The command will only give a short summary and hence won’t flood the command line.

mcqs.question: What does the following series of commands “Router IGRP 71 network” accomplish? 10.0.0.0 router IGRP 109 network 172.68.7.0

options.b: b) It loads IGRP for networks 109 and 71
options.d: d) It disables all routing protocols

mcqs.explanation: It isolates network 10.0.0.0 and 172.68.7.0 and associates autonomous systems 109 and71 with IGRP. IGRP does not disable RIP, both can be used at the same time.

mcqs.question: The “IPX delay number” command will allow an administrator to change the default settings. What are the default settings?

options.a: a) For LAN interfaces, one tick; for WAN interfaces, six ticks
options.b: b) For LAN interfaces, six ticks; for WAN interfaces, one tick
options.c: c) For LAN interfaces, zero ticks; for WAN interfaces, five ticks
options.d: d) For LAN interfaces, five ticks; for WAN interfaces, zero Ticks

mcqs.answer: a) For LAN interfaces, one tick; for WAN interfaces, six ticks
mcqs.explanation: Tick is basically the update rate of clients in the network. The IPX delay number will give the ticks at a certain time. The default ticks are–for LAN interfaces, one tick, and for WAN interfaces, six ticks.

mcqs.question: As a system administrator, you need to set up one Ethernet interface on the Cisco router to allow for both sap and Novell-ether encapsulations. Which set of commands will accomplish this?

options.a:
a) Interface Ethernet 0.1 IPX encapsulation Novell-ether IPX network 9e interface
Ethernet 0.2 IPX network 6c
options.b:
b) Interface Ethernet 0 IPX encapsulation Novell-ether IPX network 9e interface
Ethernet 0 IPX encapsulation sap IPX network 6c
options.c:
c) Interface Ethernet 0.1 IPX encapsulation Novell-ether interface Ethernet 0.2 IPX
encapsulation sap
options.d:
d) Interface Ethernet 0.1ipx encapsulation Novell-ether IPX network 9e interface
Ethernet 0.2 IPX encapsulation sap IPX network 6c

mcqs.answer:
d) Interface Ethernet 0.1ipx encapsulation Novell-ether IPX network 9e interface
Ethernet 0.2 IPX encapsulation sap IPX network 6c
mcqs.explanation: The following commands setup the sub interfaces to allow for two types of encapsulation:interface Ethernet 0.1 IPX encapsulation Novell-ether IPX network 9e interface Ethernet0.2 IPX encapsulation sap IPX network 6c.

mcqs.question: What does the “IPX maximum-paths 2” command accomplish?

options.a: a) It enables load sharing on 2 paths if the paths are equal metric paths
options.b: b) It sets up routing to go to network 2
options.c: c) It is the default for Cisco IPX load sharing
options.d: d) It enables load sharing on 2 paths if the paths are unequal metric paths

mcqs.answer: a) It enables load sharing on 2 paths if the paths are equal metric paths
mcqs.explanation: It enables load sharing on 2 paths if the paths are equal metric paths. The default is 1 path and the maximum is 512 paths. The value must always be greater than 1 and must be a natural number.

mcqs.question: You want to enable both arpa and snap encapsulation on one router interface. How do you do this?

options.a: a) The interface can handle multiple encapsulation types with no extra configuration
options.b: b) Assign two network numbers, one for each encapsulation type
options.c: c) Enable Novell-ether to run multiple encapsulation types
options.d: d) Both arpa and snap are enabled by default so you don’t have to configure anything

mcqs.answer: b) Assign two network numbers, one for each encapsulation type
mcqs.explanation: To assign multiple network numbers, you usually use sub interfaces. A sample configuration follows: IPXEthernet 0.1 IPX encapsulation novell-ether ipx network 9e interface ethernet 0.2 ipx encapsulation sap ipx network 6c

mcqs.question: By default, Cisco routers forward GNS SAPs to remote networks.
mcqs.explanation: GNS is Novell’s protocol to Get Nearest Server. If there is a server on the local network,that server will respond. If there isn’t, the Cisco router has to be configured to forward theGNS SAP.

mcqs.question: To prevent Service Advertisements (SAPs) from flooding a network, Cisco routers do not forward them. How are services advertised to other networks?

options.a: a) Each router builds its own SAP table and forwards that every 60 seconds
options.b: b) Each router assigns a service number and broadcasts that
options.c: c) SAPs aren’t necessary with Cisco routers
options.d: d) Cisco routers filter out all SAPs

mcqs.answer: a) Each router builds its own SAP table and forwards that every 60 seconds
mcqs.explanation: Cisco routers build SAP tables and forward the table every 60 seconds. All SAPs can’t befiltered even with 4.x since NDS and time synchronization uses SAPs.

mcqs.question: Novell’s implementation of RIP updates routing tables every _________ seconds.
mcqs.explanation: Novell’s RIP updates routing tables every 60 seconds, Apple’s RTMP is every 10 seconds, routers ARP every 60 seconds, IGRP signal every 90 seconds, and Banyan VINES signals every 90 seconds.

mcqs.question: In Novell’s use of RIP, there are two metrics used to make routing decisions. Select the correct metrics.
mcqs.explanation: It first uses ticks (which is about 1/18 sec.); if there is a tie, it uses hops; if hops are equal, then it uses an administratively assigned tiebreaker.

links.context: This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “RIP v1”.

mcqs.question: Which routing protocol has a maximum network diameter (hop count) of 15?
mcqs.explanation: Both RIPv1 and RIPv2 support a maximum hop count of 15 because they use 4-bits to store this value. RIPv1 uses classful routing whereas RIPv2 uses classless routing. The routing updates are broadcasted over the network. It notifies routers about the update so that they update their own routing tables.

mcqs.question: How often does a RIPv1 router broadcast its routing table by default?

options.d: d) RIPv1 does not broadcast periodically

mcqs.explanation: RIPv1 router broadcasts its routing table every 30 seconds by default. The broadcasted routing table can be used by other routers to find the shortest path among the network devices.

mcqs.question: Which command displays RIP routing updates?
mcqs.explanation: The debug IP rip command is used to show the Internet Protocol (IP) Routing Information Protocol (RIP) updates being sent and received on the router. It verifies that the updates are being broadcasted and not multicasted.

mcqs.question: Two connected routers are configured with RIP routing. What will be the result when a router receives a routing update that contains a higher-cost path to a network already in its routing table?

options.a: a) The updated information will be added to the existing routing table Debug IP rip
options.b: b) The update will be ignored and no further action will occur Debug IP route
options.c: c) The updated information will replace the existing routing table entry
options.d: d) The existing routing table entry will be deleted from the routing table and all routers will exchange routing updates to reach convergence

mcqs.answer: b) The update will be ignored and no further action will occur Debug IP route
mcqs.explanation: When a routing update is received by a router, the router first checks the administrative distance (AD) and always chooses the route with the lowest AD.
