mcqs.question: Control of users’ access to network resources through charges is the main responsibility of ______________
mcqs.explanation: Control of users’ access to network resources through charges is the main responsibility of accounting management. The accounting management creates a log of the users activity on the network too and goes hand-in-hand with the configurations management.

mcqs.question: The physical connection between an end point and a switch or between two switches is __________
mcqs.explanation: The physical connection between an end point and a switch or between two switches is transmission path. The transmission path is the physical roadway that the packet needs to propagate in order to travel through the network.

mcqs.question: Which of the following networks supports pipelining effect?
mcqs.explanation: Packet switched network is most preferred for pipelining process. Pipelining exponentially reduces the time taken to transmit a large number of packets in the network.

mcqs.question: In Network Management System, maps track each piece of hardware and its connection to the _________
mcqs.explanation: Network is the main entity connecting different components in a place. A network map is made to track each component and its connection to the network to ensure better network management.

mcqs.question: MIB is a collection of groups of objects that can be managed by __________
mcqs.explanation: MIB stands for Management Information Base. Simple network management controls the group of objects in management information base. It is usually used with SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol).

mcqs.question: A network management system can be divided into ___________
mcqs.explanation:
The five broad categories of network management are
• Fault Management
• Configuration Management
• Accounting (Administration)
• Performance Management
• Security Management.

links.context: This set of Computer Network Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Network Management Standards”.

mcqs.question: ____________ is a network management protocol that is specified in the OSI Model.
mcqs.explanation: Common Management Information Protocol (CMIP) is a standard that was introduced as a substitute for Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP). CMIP is used along with Common Management Information Services (CMIS) as an OSI Standard protocol. Thus it is specified in the OSI Model.

mcqs.question: Which one of these is a Management notification service made available by Common Management Information Service Element (CMISE)?
mcqs.explanation: There are a number of services made available by Common Management Information Service Element (CMISE). M-EVENT REPORT is a management notification service. It is used for sending notifications of managed object events to the user. Services like M-ACTION, M-DELETE, and M-CANCEL-GET are management operation services that are used to send information about system operations to users.

mcqs.question: The managed objects are defined as ___________ objects in SNMP.
mcqs.explanation: In SNMP, there are two types of managed objects: Scalar objects and Tabular Objects. In SNMP, major operations are applied to scalar objects. The major difference between scalar and tabular object is that the former has one instance and the latter has multiple instances.

mcqs.question: The IEEE standards for Local Area Network (LAN) and Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) specifications are concerned with OSI layers __________ and _________
mcqs.explanation: There are a set of IEEE standards that are used for network management. IEEE 802 standards are defined in Physical and Data Link Layers of OSI Model. It defines protocols, services etc. for Local Area Network (LAN), Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) and other Wireless Networks.

mcqs.question: The three architectures of TMN are ____________

options.a: a) Centralized architecture, Decentralized architecture, and Hierarchical architecture
options.b: b) Tiered architecture, Peer-to-peer architecture, and Client/Server architecture
options.c: c) Security architecture, Physical architecture, and Logical Layered architecture
options.d: d) Peer-to-peer architecture, Security architecture, and Centralized architecture.

mcqs.answer: c) Security architecture, Physical architecture, and Logical Layered architecture
mcqs.explanation: TMN architecture can be divided into three perspectives and those are Security architecture, Physical architecture, and Logical Layered architecture. Network management architecture consists of a Network Management system (NMS), Network Management protocol, Managed devices, Management agents and Management Information. Tiered architecture, Peer-to-peer architecture, and Client/Server architecture are the three types of Network architecture. Centralized architecture, Decentralized architecture, and Hierarchical architecture are architectures of Database Management System.

mcqs.question: There are four logical layers of TMN wherein the Service Management Layer ____________

options.a: a) analyzes business aspects, trends and billing options
options.b: b) performs configuration, control, and distributes network resources
options.c: c) handles network elements, network information and helps in maintenance
options.d: d) handles administration, information and charges of service in a network

mcqs.answer: d) handles administration, information and charges of service in a network
mcqs.explanation: TMN has four logical layers that are based on the network management services: business, network, service, and element. These layers are Business Management, Network Management, Service Management, and Element Management. Thus, Service Management Layer looks after services in a network and its administration.

mcqs.question: __________ is used to establish association between two network entities.
mcqs.explanation: Association Control Service Element (ACSE) is used for establishing as well as releasing associations between two network entities. Whereas Remote Operation Service Element (ROSE) is used for remote operations and helps in interaction between network entities in a distributed system. SMTP is a set of standards that allows transmission of electronic mail over internet. ICMP, on the other hand, is a protocol standard used for notifying error messages to the network devices.

mcqs.question: Telecomm Network Management is a protocol model that is adopted by ANSI.
mcqs.explanation: Telecomm Network Management Standards are defined by the International Telecommunication Unit (ITU-T). Whereas IEEE standards were adopted by the American National Standards Institute (ANSI).

mcqs.question: XML based network management uses _____________ technology for network management.
mcqs.explanation: Extensible Markup Language (XML) Technologies are used in XML based network management. It is used along with SNMP in order to resolve management of network elements in an ad- hoc manner. It resolves the problem of configuration management faced in SNMP. Whereas Cascading style Sheet (CSS) is a language used for styling web pages. JavaScript Notation (JSON), on the other hand, is somewhat similar to XML and is used for serializing data. Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) is used for building web applications.

mcqs.question: CMIP and SNMP protocols use IEEE standards for the upper layers.
mcqs.explanation: CMIP standards are specified in the OSI Model and SNMP is specified in the Internet Model. The IEEE specifications define the standards for the various physical media and data link protocols. Therefore CMIP and SNMP protocols use IEEE standards for the lower layers of the OSI Model.

links.context: This set of Computer Network Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Network Management Models”.

mcqs.question: OSI Network Management Model comprises of four models, they are ____________

options.a: a) organization model, information model, communication model and functional model
options.b: b) security model, peer-to-peer model, centralized model, and decentralized model
options.c: c) tiered model, hierarchical model, client/server model, logical layered model
options.d: d) centralized model, decentralized model, physical model, and hierarchical model

mcqs.answer: b) security model, peer-to-peer model, centralized model, and decentralized model
mcqs.explanation: OSI network management model is governed by ISO standards. It is superior to most other models. The OSI network Management Model can be classified further into four models such as organization model, information model, communication model and functional model. Whereas tiered model, hierarchical model, client/server model, logical layered model, centralized model, decentralized model, physical model, security model and peer-to-peer model are types of architecture of TNM.

mcqs.question: The architecture for SNMP standard for network management is defined by _________
mcqs.explanation: IETF stands for Internet Engineering Task Force. It is a set of standards that implicitly defines the architecture for SNMP. SNMP network management is used for campus wide networks.

mcqs.question: Simple Network Management Protocol is designed for management of Telecommunication networks only.
mcqs.explanation: SNMP is used for managing Wide Area Networks (WAN) as well as Telecomm systems. Telecomm Management Network (TMN) on the other hand deals with Telecomm service providers only.

mcqs.question: The fourth component of Network Management, functional model, deals with ___________

options.a: a) the user-oriented requirements of network management
options.b: b) the structure and organization of management information
options.c: c) the components of a network management system
options.d: d) the layer operation within the layers.

mcqs.answer: a) the user-oriented requirements of network management
mcqs.explanation: The OSI network Management Model can be classified further into four models such as organization model, information model, communication model and functional model. The functional model deals with user-oriented requirements of Network management. Whereas Information model looks after the structure and organization of management information. The organization model deals with the components of a network management system and its functions. Lastly, the operation of layers in the application layer occurs in the communication model.

mcqs.question: What is the function of SMI?

options.a: a) It deals with the storage of management information
options.b: b) It addresses operation and administration of functional model
options.c: c) It describes how the management information is structured
options.d: d) It provides a complete model for network management

mcqs.answer: c) It describes how the management information is structured
mcqs.explanation: The information model of the OSI network management deals with Structured Management Information (SMI) and information database known as Management Information Base (MIB). Here the SMI helps in defining the structure of management information.

mcqs.question: Applications developed under Web-based management falls under the OSI ______ model.
mcqs.explanation: The OSI network Management Model can be classified further into four models such as organization model, information model, communication model and functional model. Thus, in Web-based management, the applications developed falls under the functional model of OSI network management.

mcqs.question: Configuration, fault, performance, security, and accounting are the system management functions of SNMP.
mcqs.explanation: Configuration, fault, performance, security and accounting are the four functional areas of OSI network management. SNMP is the standard that manages WAN and telecomm systems.

links.context: This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Network Utilities”.

mcqs.question: Ping can _________
mcqs.explanation: PING (Packet Internet Groper) command is the best way to test connectivity between two nodes, whether it is Local Area Network (LAN) or Wide Area Network (WAN). Ping uses ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol) to communicate to other devices.

mcqs.question: Ping sweep is a part of _________
mcqs.explanation: A ping sweep is a method that can establish a range of IP addresses which map to live hosts and are mostly used by network scanning tools like nmap. A ping sweep is basically a collective ping command execution on a range of IP addresses.

mcqs.question: ICMP is used in _________
mcqs.explanation: ICMP stands for Internet Control Message Protocol. ICMP operates over the IP packet to provide error reporting functionality, so in case the node is not active or there is no route, ICMP will be used to report the specific errors for Ping and Traceroute.

mcqs.question: __________ command is used to manipulate TCP/IP routing table.
mcqs.explanation: The route command is used to view and manipulate the TCP/IP routing table in Windows OS. The manipulations done in the routing table with the help of this command will count as static routes.

mcqs.question: If you want to find the number of routers between a source and destination, the utility to be used is ___________
mcqs.explanation: Traceroute command is available on Linux OS to find the path i.e. the number of the routers that the packet has to go through to reach the destination. In Windows, Tracert command is used to perform the function.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not related to ipconfig in Microsoft Windows?

options.a: a) Display all current TCP/IP network configuration values
options.d: d) Trace the routers in the path to destination

mcqs.answer: d) Trace the routers in the path to destination
mcqs.explanation: The Tracert command is available on Microsoft Windows to find the path i.e. the number of the routers that the packet has to go through to reach its destination.

mcqs.question: __________ allows checking if a domain is available for registration.
mcqs.explanation: There are billions of domains available for registration on the World Wide Web, and many of them are already registered. So when one wants to register a domain, they need to check whether the domain is available through a domain check.

mcqs.question: Choose the wrong statement from the following.

options.a: a) Nslookup is used to query a DNS server for DNS data
options.b: b) Ping is used to check connectivity
options.c: c) Pathping combines the functionality of ping with that of route
options.d: d) Ifconfig can configure TCP/IP network interface parameters

mcqs.answer: c) Pathping combines the functionality of ping with that of route
mcqs.explanation: Pathping combines the functionality of ping with that of traceroute (tracert). The Ping command is used to test connectivity between two nodes and the Tracert/Traceroute command is used to find the path i.e. the number of the routers that the packet has to go through to reach its destination.

links.context:
This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Error Detection and Correction Techniques”.

Technical Primer for this Topic: Error Detection in Computer Networks

mcqs.question: What is the hamming distance between the words 1010101, 1100110?
mcqs.explanation: Hamming distance can be obtained by performing X-OR operation on two words of same length, then the number of 1s in the resulting word will be the hamming distance. It is used to find and correct the errors.

mcqs.question: What is the disadvantage of the burst errors over single bit errors in error detection and correction?
mcqs.explanation: The burst errors can be detected easily but it is difficult to correct them, as they happen to appear as blocks. When the error rate is low, burst errors are convenient to detect compared to single bit errors.

mcqs.question: What is the minimum hamming distance between the words 0001, 0100, 0110, 1111?
mcqs.explanation: In order to find the minimum hamming distance between the set of words, the hamming distance between all pairs of the set should be calculated. The least number in the resulted hamming distances will be the minimum hamming distance.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an error correcting code?
mcqs.explanation: Hamming code assigns consecutive numbers for code word; the code word will have check bits in place of the numbers that are powers of 2 and the remaining numbers contain bits of data word.

mcqs.question: An error is burst error, if two or more consecutive bits of the data unit are corrupted.
mcqs.explanation: An error is considered as a burst error, if two or more bits get corrupted, but they don’t need to be consecutive bits. Length of the burst independent of sequence, that is length between first burst bit to last burst bit is considered as length of burst.

mcqs.question: How many bits will be added to a data word to become a code word in simple parity check code?
mcqs.explanation: Code word will have total of k+1 bits where k is the number of bits in data word. This extra parity bit helps the code word to have even number of 1s and it can be 0 or 1. Parity code is an error detecting code but doesn’t correct the errors.

mcqs.question: Which of the following error correcting code is not a linear bock code?
mcqs.explanation: Unlike block codes, convolution codes don’t have encoding boundary. The encoder in this convolution codes deals with sequence of bits and outputs sequence of bits using constraint length of the code.

mcqs.question: Which error correcting code works well for burst errors among the following?
mcqs.explanation: Hamming codes and convolution codes works well for single bit errors, whereas Reed Solomon codes works well for burst errors. Because it uses m bit symbols, which are used to treat single bit and m bit burst errors equally as a single symbol error.

mcqs.question: What is the maximum number of errors that can be detected using two-dimensional parity check code?
mcqs.explanation: Two-dimensional parity check was introduced to overcome the problem in simple parity check code that it is able to find only odd numbers of errors. Two-dimensional parity arranges the code into columns and rows and add parity bits in each column and row to find errors up to 3.

mcqs.question: Simple parity-check is used to detect the even number of errors also.
mcqs.explanation: Simple parity check uses only one bit for parity and the bit that is added to a data word can detect odd number of errors only. Because, the even parity will be same after even number of errors occur and it shows no error.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an error detecting code?
mcqs.explanation: Given all codes are error detecting codes other than hamming code. Error detecting codes are used for noisy and wireless links whereas error correcting codes are used for channels like optical fiber.

mcqs.question: How cyclic redundancy check code can also be called?
mcqs.explanation: Polynomial codes has the polynomial representation for bit strings and these polynomials have 0 or 1 as their coefficients. It makes use of generator polynomial to do further calculation in finding errors.

links.context:
This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Multiple Access Links and Protocols”.

Foundational Reading for this Topic: Channel Allocation Problem in Computer Network

mcqs.question: Which of the following are the types of basic protocols that are present in multiple access control in data link layer?
mcqs.explanation: In random access control protocol, the medium can be shared randomly depending on the state of the medium. In controlled access, stations share the medium depending on authorization. Channelization allows the stations to share the bandwidth of the link.

mcqs.question: Which aspect of the random-access protocols makes them contention methods?

options.a: a) No rules for accessing medium

mcqs.answer: a) No rules for accessing medium
mcqs.explanation: Random access protocol also called as contention methods have no rules or time for stations to place their frames on the medium. For this reason, stations compete among themselves for accessing the medium.

mcqs.question: Why station need to wait random amount of time for re-transmission of the frame after collision in pure aloha?

options.d: d) To get acknowledgment from the receiver

mcqs.explanation: Collision includes two more stations, if those stations again re-transmit the frames at a time; it causes collision again. Back-off time is to avoid this collision by making the stations to wait for some random times.

mcqs.question: Which strategy is used by the pure aloha to prevent the congestion caused by continuous re-transmitted frames?

options.a: a) Aborts the re-transmission after 5 attempts
options.b: b) A station is allowed to re-transmit for 2 times
options.c: c) Restriction on the attempts for re-transmission

mcqs.answer: c) Restriction on the attempts for re-transmission
mcqs.explanation: If a station re-transmits a frame more than the times, that is defined by the pure aloha, then pure aloha will abort the process re-transmission of the particular frame. The station needs to try after sometime later to send the frames.

mcqs.question: What is the vulnerable time of the pure aloha for fixed length of frames (T=frame time)?
mcqs.explanation: Vulnerable time is time in which, there is a possibility for a collision. T(frame) is the time taken by a frame to be sent to destination. Vulnerable time will be 2 times the fixed length of frames.

mcqs.question: Which of the following controlled access protocol is known as master slave method?
mcqs.explanation: Polling is the method for channel allocation where one station acts as a server and remaining stations acts according to the decision of master station. This master station also known as primary device, which uses two functions called poll function and select function to send and receive data within the network.

mcqs.question: Which of the following type of multiple access protocols uses a scheme called “Authorization from other stations”?
mcqs.explanation: In controlled access protocols, stations send frames only if they get the authorization from the other stations to use the channel. This authorization can be obtained using methods such as reservation, polling, token passing.

mcqs.question: Which of the following persistent method of random-access protocol reduces the collisions and efficiency of the network?
mcqs.explanation: Unlike 1- persistent in non-persistent methods, stations wait for some random time even if it finds the channel idle. This random time reduces the collision at the same time it reduces the efficiency because random times may keep the channel unused even the stations have frames to send.

mcqs.question: What is the vulnerable time in carrier sense multiple access?
mcqs.explanation: In carrier sense multiple access, the stations sense the medium whether it is idle or not. This information is sent by the station which is using the medium, using propagation of a signal. The propagation delay in the signal causes the collision.

mcqs.question: Slotted aloha has vulnerable time that is half of the vulnerable time of pure aloha.
mcqs.explanation: In slotted aloha, the time is divided into time slots, that are of T(frame) length. The stations are instructed to send the frames at the starting of the time slot. Still there is a chance for collision, if 2 frames are started at the same it. This is why vulnerable time is equal to the time taken by a frame to be sent to the destination.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a channelization protocol?
mcqs.explanation: The channelization protocols use frequency, time and code to divide the bandwidth of the channel. Bandwidth is divided into frequency bands in FDMA, same bandwidth is used by the stations in TDMA.

mcqs.question: What technique is used by the TDMA to accomplish synchronization?
mcqs.explanation: Time division multiple access allocates the time slots for station to use the channel. These time slots are synchronized by preamble bits, which acts as guard time between two time slots.

links.context: This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “MAC Address”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a name for MAC(Media Access Control) in data link layer?
mcqs.explanation: MAC(media access control)address will be assigned to NIC(Network Interface Controller). These addresses are assigned by the manufacture of those particular devices and are unique. Logical address is the IP address of the network.

mcqs.question: What is the size of MAC address in medium access control sub layer?
mcqs.explanation: MAC address is a 48 bit with 6 octets and can be represented as EUI-48. As MAC address is a 48 bit space, 248 MAC addresses are possible. Non-Ethernet applications can have EUI-64 address.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a separator to be used in MAC address?
mcqs.explanation: These separators are chosen by manufacturer, who manufactures the device. Hyphen is used by MICROSOFT, period(.) is used by CISCO, colon(:) is used by LINUX. Dollar is not used as a separator.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the correct sentence about MAC address?
mcqs.explanation: IP address is represented in decimals (10.10.25.44), whereas, MAC address is represented in hexadecimal(60-30-74-00-ED-FC). The MAC address has total of 6 octets and each octet has 8 bits that is 2 hexadecimal numbers(48bits).

mcqs.question: What is the primary use of MAC filtering on wireless networks?
mcqs.explanation: MAC filtering allows only approved MAC addresses to send traffic in the network. It provides security, even if hacker hijacks the IP address. Because, the hacker will not be allowed into network without approved MAC address.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a type of MAC address?
mcqs.explanation: MAC address can be UNICAST, MULTICAST or BROADCAST. If LSB(least significant bit) is zero(0) of first octet of the MAC address, then it is uni-cast. LSB is one(1) for multicast and one(1) in all bits of the address is broadcast.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a similarity between MAC and IP address?

options.c: c) Every device should have it
options.d: d) Both Operates on data link layer

mcqs.answer: d) Both Operates on data link layer
mcqs.explanation: MAC addresses are used by the switch in the data link layer, whereas IP addresses are used by the router in network layer. IP address will change depending upon network in which the device is present but, MAC address is constant.

mcqs.question: Which of the following hardware in our computer is embedded with MAC address?
mcqs.explanation: NIC(network interface card) knows only about MAC address which is embedded in it. It doesn’t know about IP address and it is the only hardware in the device which is aware of network communication.

mcqs.question: How many octets are dedicated to OUI(Organizationally unique identifier) in in 48 MAC address space?
mcqs.explanation: OUI is the address that is universally administered and identifies the the device uniquely. Out of six octets, three octets are used to identify the OUI, that to which organization it belongs.

mcqs.question: Nodes in a network(router) has only one MAC address in the network.
mcqs.explanation: A network node can have number of MAC addresses based on the number of interfaces. Network node has unique MAC address for each interface(NIC). But it is possible for two NICs to share MAC address, which are connected to different networks.

links.context:
This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Ethernet”.

Technical Primer for this Topic: What is Ethernet?

mcqs.question: Ethernet frame consists of ____________
mcqs.explanation: The Ethernet frame has a header that contains the source and destination MAC address. Each MAC address is of 48 bits.

mcqs.question: What is start frame delimeter (SFD) in ethernet frame?
mcqs.explanation: The start frame delimiter is a 1 byte field in the Ethernet frame that indicates that the preceding bits are the start of the frame. It is always set to 10101011.

mcqs.question: MAC address is of ___________
mcqs.explanation: MAC address is like a local address for the NIC that is used to make a local Ethernet (or wifi) network function. It is of 48 bits.

mcqs.question: What is autonegotiation?

options.a: a) a procedure by which two connected devices choose common transmission parameters

mcqs.answer: a) a procedure by which two connected devices choose common transmission parameters
mcqs.explanation: autonegotiation is a procedure by which two connected devices choose common transmission parameters. It is a signaling mechanism used in Ethernet over Twisted pair cables.

mcqs.question: Ethernet in metropolitan area network (MAN) can be used as ___________
mcqs.explanation: A metropolitan area network (MAN) that is based on Ethernet standards is called an Ethernet MAN. It is commonly used to connect nodes to the Internet. Businesses also use Ethernet MANs to connect their own offices to each other.

mcqs.question: A point-to-point protocol over ethernet is a network protocol for __________

options.a: a) encapsulating PPP frames inside ethernet frames
options.b: b) encapsulating ehternet framse inside PPP frames
options.c: c) for security of ethernet frames
options.d: d) for security of PPP frames

mcqs.answer: a) encapsulating PPP frames inside ethernet frames
mcqs.explanation: PPoE or Point-to-Point protocol over Ethernet was first introduced in 1999. It is popularly used by modern day Internet Service Providers for Dial-up connectivity.

mcqs.question: High speed ethernet works on _________
mcqs.explanation: Fast Ethernet is mostly used in networks along with Category 5 (Cat-5) copper twisted-pair cable, but it also works with fiber-optic cable. Based on the cable being used, There can be three types of Fast Ethernet.

mcqs.question: The maximum size of payload field in ethernet frame is __________
mcqs.explanation: The minimum size of the payload field is 40 bytes and the maximum size is 1500 bytes. If the payload size exceeds 1500 bytes, the frame is called a jumbo frame.

mcqs.question: What is interframe gap?

options.b: b) idle time between frame bits

mcqs.explanation: The inter-frame gap is the idle time for the receiver between the incoming frame flow. The inter-frame gap must be as low as possible for idle connections.

mcqs.question: An ethernet frame that is less than the IEEE 802.3 minimum length of 64 octets is called _______
mcqs.explanation: An ethernet frame that is less than the IEEE 802.3 minimum length of 64 octets is called a runt frame. Such frames are a result of collisions or software malfunctions.

title: 10. Computer Network MCQ on Wireless LAN’s, Electronic Mail and File Transfer

links.context:
This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Wireless LAN”.

Technical Prep Guide for this Topic: Wireless Security

mcqs.question: What is the access point (AP) in a wireless LAN?

options.a: a) device that allows wireless devices to connect to a wired network
options.c: c) both device that allows wireless devices to connect to a wired network and wireless devices itself
options.d: d) all the nodes in the network

mcqs.answer: a) device that allows wireless devices to connect to a wired network
mcqs.explanation: Access point in a wireless network is any device that will allow the wireless devices to a wired network. A router is the best example of an Access Point.

mcqs.question: In wireless ad-hoc network _________

options.a: a) access point is not required
options.d: d) all nodes are access points

mcqs.answer: a) access point is not required
mcqs.explanation: An ad-hoc wireless network is a decentralized kind of a wireless network. An access point is usually a central device and it would go against the rules of the ad-hoc network to use one. Hence it is not required.

mcqs.question: Which multiple access technique is used by IEEE 802.11 standard for wireless LAN?
mcqs.explanation: CSMA/CA stands for Carrier-sense multiple access/collision avoidance. It is a multiple access protocol used by IEEE 802.11 standard for wireless LAN. It’s based on the principle of collision avoidance by using different algorithms to avoid collisions between channels.

mcqs.question: In wireless distribution system __________

options.a: a) multiple access point are inter-connected with each other
options.b: b) there is no access point
options.c: c) only one access point exists
options.d: d) access points are not required

mcqs.answer: a) multiple access point are inter-connected with each other
mcqs.explanation: A Wireless Distribution System allows the connection of multiple access points together. It is used to expand a wireless network to a larger network.

mcqs.question: A wireless network interface controller can work in _______

options.c: c) both infrastructure mode and ad-hoc mode

mcqs.answer: c) both infrastructure mode and ad-hoc mode
mcqs.explanation: A wireless network interface controller works on the physical layer and the data link layer of the OSI model. Infrastructure mode WNIC needs access point but in ad-hoc mode access point is not required.

mcqs.question: In wireless network an extended service set is a set of ________
mcqs.explanation: The extended service set is a part of the IEEE 802.11 WLAN architecture and is used to expand the range of the basic service set by allowing connection of multiple basic service sets.

mcqs.question: Mostly ________ is used in wireless LAN.
mcqs.explanation: In orthogonal frequency division multiplexing, digital data is encoded on multiple carrier frequencies. It is also used in digital television and audio broadcasting in addition to Wireless LANs.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following event is not possible in wireless LAN?
mcqs.explanation: Collision detection is not possible in wireless LAN with no extensions. Collision detection techniques for multiple access like CSMA/CD are used to detect collisions in Wireless LANs.

mcqs.question: What is Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP)?

options.b: b) security algorithm for wireless networks
options.c: c) security algorithm for usb communication

mcqs.answer: b) security algorithm for wireless networks
mcqs.explanation: WEP is a security algorithm for wireless network which intended to provide data confidentiality comparable to that of traditional wired networks. It was introduced in 1997.

mcqs.question: What is WPA?
mcqs.explanation: WPA or WiFi Protected Access is a security protocol used to provide users and firms with strong data security and protection for their wireless networks (WiFi) to give them confidence that only authorized users can access their network.

links.context: This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Internet”.

mcqs.question: What is internet?

options.b: b) A collection of unrelated computers
options.c: c) interconnection of local area networks
options.d: d) interconnection of wide area networks

mcqs.answer: d) interconnection of wide area networks
mcqs.explanation: The internet is a global network formed by connecting wide area networks (WANs), enabling worldwide communication and data sharing.

mcqs.question: To join the internet, the computer has to be connected to a _________
mcqs.explanation: The ISPs (Internet Service Providers) are the main agents through which every computer is connected to the internet. They are licensed to allot public IP addresses to its customers in order to connect them to the internet.

mcqs.question: Internet access by transmitting digital data over the wires of a local telephone network is provided by _______
mcqs.explanation: DSL (Digital Subscriber Line) is the technology designed to use the existing telephone lines to transport high-bandwidth data to service subscribers. DSL was used to allow the early users access to the internet and it provides dedicated, point-to-point, public network access.

mcqs.question: ISP exchanges internet traffic between their networks by __________
mcqs.explanation: ISPs exchange internet traffic between their networks by using Internet Exchange Points. ISPs and CDNs are connected to each other at these physical locations are they help them provide better service to their customers.

mcqs.question: Which of the following protocols is used in the internet?
mcqs.explanation: HTTP is used to browse all the websites on the World Wide Web, DHCP is used to allot IPs automatically to the users on the internet, and DNS is used to connect the users to the host servers on the internet based on the Domain Name.

mcqs.question: The size of an IP address in IPv6 is _________
mcqs.explanation: An IPv6 address is 128 bits long. Therefore, 2128 i.e. 340 undecillion addresses are possible in IPv6. IPv4 has only 4 billion possible addresses and IPv6 would be a brilliant alternative in case IPv4 runs out of possible new addresses.

mcqs.question: Internet works on _______

options.c: c) both packet switching and circuit switching

mcqs.explanation: Packet switching is the method based on which the internet works. Packet switching features delivery of packets of data between devices over a shared network.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not an application layer protocol used in internet?
mcqs.explanation: Resource reservation protocol is a transport layer protocol used on the internet. It operates over IPv4 and IPv6 and is designed to reserve resources required by the network layer protocols.

mcqs.question: Which protocol assigns IP address to the client connected in the internet?
mcqs.explanation: DHCP stands for Domain Host Control Protocol. It is responsible to remotely assign IP address to the clients connected to the internet. The server that performs this fuction is called the DHCP server.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not used in media access control?
mcqs.explanation: Packet switching is not really related to media access control as it just features delivery of packets of data between devices over a shared network. Internet is actually based on packet switching.

links.context:
This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Bluetooth”.

Technical Prep Guide for this Topic: Wireless Security

mcqs.question: An interconnected collection of piconet is called ___________
mcqs.explanation: Piconet is the basic unit of a bluetooth system having a master node and upto seven active slave nodes. A collection of piconets is called scatternet and a slave node of a piconet may act as a master in a piconet that is part of the scatternet.

mcqs.question: In a piconet, there can be up to ________ parked nodes in the network.
mcqs.explanation: A slave node in a piconet can be instructed by the master node to go into parked mode. Then the slave node enters the parked mode in which the node is not disconnected from the network but is inactive unless the master wakes it up.

mcqs.question: Bluetooth is the wireless technology for __________
mcqs.explanation: Bluetooth is a wireless technology used to create a wireless personal area network for data transfer up to a distance of 10 meters. It operates on 2.45 GHz frequency band for transmission.

mcqs.question: Bluetooth uses __________
mcqs.explanation: Frequency hopping spread spectrum is a method of transmitting radio signals by rapidly changing the carrier frequency and is controlled by the codes known to the sender and receiver only.

mcqs.question: Unauthorised access of information from a wireless device through a bluetooth connection is called _________
mcqs.explanation: Unauthorised access of information from a wireless device through a bluetooth connection is called Bluesnarfing. It is done through exploiting the vulnerabilities of the Bluetooth device to steal the transmitted information.

mcqs.question: What is A2DP (advanced audio distribution profile)?

options.a: a) a bluetooth profile for streaming audio
options.b: b) a bluetooth profile for streaming video
options.c: c) a bluetooth profile for security
options.d: d) a bluetooth profile for file management

mcqs.answer: a) a bluetooth profile for streaming audio
mcqs.explanation: A2DP stands for Advanced Audio Distribution Profile is a transfer standard use to transmit high definition audio through Bluetooth. It is mainly used in Bluetooth speakers and wireless headphones.

mcqs.question: In a piconet, one master device ________

options.b: b) can be slave in another piconet
options.c: c) can be slave in the same piconet
options.d: d) can be master in another piconet

mcqs.answer: b) can be slave in another piconet
mcqs.explanation: In a scatternet, a slave node of one piconet may act as a master in a piconet that is part of the scatternet. The scatternet uses this property to connect many piconets together to create a larger network.

mcqs.question: Bluetooth transceiver devices operate in ______ band.
mcqs.explanation: Bluetooth operates on 2.45 GHz frequency ISM band for transmission. It is used to create a wireless personal area network for data transfer up to a distance of 10 meters.

mcqs.question: Bluetooth supports _______

options.c: c) both point-to-point connections and point-to-multipoint connection

mcqs.answer: c) both point-to-point connections and point-to-multipoint connection
mcqs.explanation: In Bluetooth, each slave node communicates with the master of the piconet independently i.e. each master-slave connection is independent. The slave is not allowed to communicate with other slaves directly.

mcqs.question: A scatternet can have maximum __________
mcqs.explanation: A scatternet can have maximum of 10 piconets and minimum of 2 piconets. To connect these piconets, a slave node of one piconet may act as a master in a piconet that is part of the scatternet.

links.context: This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “WiMAX”.

mcqs.question: WiMAX stands for ___________

options.b: b) worldwide interoperability for microwave access
options.c: c) worldwide international standard for microwave access

mcqs.answer: b) worldwide interoperability for microwave access
mcqs.explanation: WiMAX or worldwide interoperability for microwave access is a set of wireless communication standards. It provides support for multiple physical layer (PHY) and Media Access Control (MAC) options. It is based on IEEE 802.16 standards.

mcqs.question: WiMAX provides ________
mcqs.explanation: WiMax was developed to provide wireless broadband access to buildings. It can also be used to connect WLAN hotspots to the Internet. It is based on IEEE 802.16 standards.

mcqs.question: WiMAX uses the _________
mcqs.explanation: WiMAX physical layer uses orthogonal frequency division multiplexing as it provides simplified reception in multipath and allows WiMAX to operate in NLOS conditions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following modulation schemes is supported by WiMAX?

options.a: a) binary phase shift keying modulation
options.b: b) quadrature phase shift keying modulation

mcqs.explanation: WiMAX supports a variety of modulation schemes such as binary phase shift keying modulation, quadrature phase shift keying modulation, and quadrature amplitude modulation and allows for the scheme to change on a burst-by-burst basis per link, depending on channel conditions.

mcqs.question: WiMAX MAC layer provides an interface between ___________

options.a: a) higher transport layers and physical layer
options.b: b) application layer and network layer
options.c: c) data link layer and network layer
options.d: d) session layer and application layer

mcqs.answer: a) higher transport layers and physical layer
mcqs.explanation: WiMAX provides support for multiple physical layer (PHY) on the physical layer and Media Access Control (MAC) options for higher layers to provide wireless broadband access to buildings.

mcqs.question: For encryption, WiMAX supports _______

options.c: c) advanced encryption standard and triple data encryption standard

mcqs.answer: c) advanced encryption standard and triple data encryption standard
mcqs.explanation: Both advanced encryption standard and triple data encryption standard are block cipher techniques and are popularly used in WiMAX and other applications for secure encryption.

mcqs.question: WiMAX provides _______

options.c: c) Both VoIP and IPTV services

mcqs.answer: c) Both VoIP and IPTV services
mcqs.explanation: IPTV can be transmitted over WiMAX, and relies on packet-switching to offer reliable delivery. VoIP can be operated over a WiMax network with no special hardware or software.

mcqs.question: Devices that provide the connectivity to a WiMAX network are known as _________
mcqs.explanation: Subscriber stations in WiMAX are transceivers (transmitter and receivers). They are used to convert radio signals into digital signals that can be routed to and from communication devices. There is a variety of types of WiMAX subscriber stations like portable PCMCIA cards and fixed stations that provide service to multiple users.

mcqs.question: WiMAX is mostly used for __________
mcqs.explanation: WiMAX provides Wi-Fi connectivity within the home or business for computers and smartphones. WiMAX network operators typically provide a WiMAX Subscriber Unit to do so. The subscriber unit is used to connect to the metropolitan WiMAX network.

mcqs.question: Which of the following frequencies is not used in WiMAX for communication?
mcqs.explanation: The 2.4GHz ISM frequency band is used for personal area network technologies such as Bluetooth and hence is not suitable for WiMAX which is mostly used for Metropolitan Area Networks.

links.context: This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “SONET”.

mcqs.question: SONET stands for ___________
mcqs.explanation: SONET stands for synchronous optical network. Frame relay uses SONET to physically transmit data frames over a Frame Relay network as SONET is cheaper and provides better network reliability than other carriers.

mcqs.question: In SONET, STS-1 level of electrical signalling has the data rate of _________
mcqs.explanation: STS-1 level provides the data rate of 51.84 Mbps, STS-3 provides a data rate of 155.52 Mbps, STS-12 provides a data rate of 622.080 Mbps and STS-48 provides a data rate of 2488.320 Mbps.

mcqs.question: The path layer of SONET is responsible for the movement of a signal _________

options.a: a) from its optical source to its optical destination
options.d: d) back to its optical source

mcqs.answer: a) from its optical source to its optical destination
mcqs.explanation: The path layer in SONET is responsible for the movement signal from the optical source to the optical destination. It is ideally expected to find the shortest and the most reliable path to the destination.

mcqs.question: The photonic layer of the SONET is similar to the __________ of OSI model.
mcqs.explanation: The photonic layer in SONET is like the physical layer of the OSI model. It is the lowest layer among the four layers of SONET namely the photonic, the section, the line, and the path layers.

mcqs.question: In SONET, each synchronous transfer signal STS-n is composed of __________
mcqs.explanation: SONET defines the electrical signal as STS-N (Synchronous Transport Signal Level-N) and the optical signal as OC-N (Optical Carrier Level-N). The building block of SONET is the STS-1/OC-1 signal, which is based on an 8-kHz frame rate and operates at 51.84 Mbps.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not true about SONET?

options.a: a) frames of lower rate can be synchronously time-division multiplexed into a higher-rate frame
options.c: c) all clocks in the network are locked to a master clock
options.d: d) STS-1 provides the data rate of 622.080Mbps

mcqs.answer: d) STS-1 provides the data rate of 622.080Mbps
mcqs.explanation: In SONET, STS-N stands for Synchronous Transport Signal Level-N. STS-1 level provides the data rate of 51.84 Mbps, and STS-12 provides a data rate of 622.080 Mbps.

mcqs.question: A linear SONET network can be ________
mcqs.explanation: Synchronous Optical Network (SONET) is basically an optical fiber point-to-point or ring network backbone that provides a way to accommodate additional capacity as the needs of the organization increase to multipoint networks.

mcqs.question: Automatic protection switching in linear network is defined at the _______
mcqs.explanation: The Line layer in SONET operates like the data link layer in the OSI model and it is responsible for the movement of signal across a physical line. The Synchronous Transport Signal Mux/Demux and Add/Drop Mux provide the Line layer functions.

mcqs.question: A unidirectional path switching ring is a network with __________
mcqs.explanation: One ring is used as the working ring and other as the protection ring in which each node is connected to its respective adjacent nodes by two fibers, one to transmit, and one to receive.

mcqs.question: What is SDH?

options.a: a) sdh is similar standard to SONET developed by ITU-T
options.c: c) sdh stands for synchronous digital hierarchy and is a similar standard to SONET developed by ITU-T

mcqs.answer: c) sdh stands for synchronous digital hierarchy and is a similar standard to SONET developed by ITU-T
mcqs.explanation: SDH is a standard that allows low bit rates to be combined into high-rate data streams and as it is synchronous, each individual bit stream can be embedded into and extracted from high-rate data streams easily.

links.context: This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “RTP”.

mcqs.question: Real-time transport protocol (RTP) is mostly used in _________
mcqs.explanation: RTP stands for Real-time transport protocol and is for delivering audio and video over IP networks. Its applications include streaming media, video teleconference, and television services.

mcqs.question: RTP is used to ________

options.b: b) monitor transmission statistics of streams
options.c: c) monitor quality of service of streams

mcqs.explanation: RTP is used to carry the media stream for delivering audio and video over IP networks. Its applications include streaming media, video teleconference, and television services.

mcqs.question: RTP provides the facility of jitter ____________
mcqs.explanation: RTP provides the facility of jitter media stream through a jitter buffer which works by reconstructing the sequence of packets on the receiving side. Then an even audio / video stream is generated.

mcqs.question: Which protocol provides the synchronization between media streams?
mcqs.explanation: RTCP stands for Real-time Transport Control Protocol and it works with RTP to send control packets to the users of the networks while RTP handles the actual data delivery.

mcqs.question: An RTP session is established for ____________

options.c: c) some predefined number of media streams

mcqs.explanation: An RTP session is required to be established for each media stream for delivering audio and video over the IP network. Each session has independent data transmission.

mcqs.question: RTP can use __________
mcqs.explanation: RTP uses unprevileleged UDP ports, stream control transmission protocol, and datagram congestion control protocol for data delivery over IP networks.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following multimedia formats can not be supported by RTP?
mcqs.explanation: RTP is suitable only for multimedia and not for simple text files as the operation would result into wastage of resources. Other protocols like FTP are suitable for such transmissions.

mcqs.question: An RTP header has a minimum size of _________
mcqs.explanation: Each RTP packet has a fixed header of size 12 bytes that contains essential control information like timestamp, payload type etc. for the receiving system processing.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not correct?

options.a: a) RTCP provides canonical end-point identifiers to all session participants
options.b: b) RTCP reports are expected to be sent by all participants
options.c: c) RTCP itself does not provide any flow encryption or authentication methods
options.d: d) RTCP handles the actual data delivery

mcqs.answer: d) RTCP handles the actual data delivery
mcqs.explanation: RTCP works with RTP to send control packets to the users of the networks and provide canonical end-point identifiers to all session participants while RTP handles the actual data delivery.

mcqs.question: Which protocol defines a profile of RTP that provides cryptographic services for the transfer of payload data?
mcqs.explanation: SRTP stands for Secure Real-time Transport Protocol. It is like an extension to RTP which provides stream security through encryption, message authentication and integrity, and replay attack protection.

links.context: This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “RPC”.

mcqs.question: An RPC (remote procedure call) is initiated by the _________
mcqs.explanation: Remote Procedure Call is a method used for constructing distributed, client-server applications based on extending the conventional local procedure calling where the client initiates an RPC to start a connection process.

mcqs.question: In RPC, while a server is processing the call, the client is blocked ________

options.a: a) unless the client sends an asynchronous request to the server
options.b: b) unless the call processing is complete
options.c: c) for the complete duration of the connection
options.d: d) unless the server is disconnected

mcqs.answer: a) unless the client sends an asynchronous request to the server
mcqs.explanation: While the server is processing the call i.e. looking through the specifications, the client is blocked, unless the client sends an asynchronous request to the server for another operation.

mcqs.question: A remote procedure call is _______
mcqs.explanation: Remote procedure calls is a form of inter-process communication where the client initiates an RPC to start a connection process. It is used to construct distributed, client-server applications.

mcqs.question: RPC allows a computer program to cause a subroutine to execute in _________

options.c: c) both its own address space and another address space

mcqs.explanation: RPC allows a computer program to cause a subroutine to execute in another address space which is usually the servers address space in a conventional client-server network.

mcqs.question: RPC works between two processes. These processes must be ____________

options.b: b) on different computers connected with a network
options.c: c) on the same computer and also on different computers connected with a network
options.d: d) on none of the computers

mcqs.answer: c) on the same computer and also on different computers connected with a network
mcqs.explanation: For the operation of RPC between two processes, it is mandatory that the processes are present on the same computer and also on different computers connected with its network.

mcqs.question: A remote procedure is uniquely identified by _________
mcqs.explanation: Each remote procedure can be uniquely identified by the program number, version number and the procedure number in the networks scope. The identifiers can be used to control the remote procedure by parties involved in the process.

mcqs.question: An RPC application requires _________

options.a: a) specific protocol for client server communication

mcqs.explanation: The RPC technique for constructing distributed, client-server applications based on extending the conventional local procedure calling. It requires a client program, a server program and specific protocol for client server communication to build the system.

mcqs.question: RPC is used to _________

options.a: a) establish a server on remote machine that can respond to queries
options.b: b) retrieve information by calling a query
options.c: c) establish a server on remote machine that can respond to queries and retrieve information by calling a query

mcqs.answer: c) establish a server on remote machine that can respond to queries and retrieve information by calling a query
mcqs.explanation: RPC or Remote Procedure Call is used to establish a server on remote machine that can respond to queries and to retrieve information by calling a query by other computers.

mcqs.question: RPC is a _________
mcqs.explanation: RPC is a synchronous operation where the remote machine works in sync with the other machines to act as a server that can respond to queries called by the other machines.

mcqs.question: The local operating system on the server machine passes the incoming packets to the ___________
mcqs.explanation: The local operating system on the server machine passes the incoming packets to the server stub which then processes the packets which contain the queries from the client machines for retrieving information.

links.context:
This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Symmetric Key Cryptography”.

Technical Primer for this Topic: Cryptography

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an alternative name for symmetric key cryptography?
mcqs.explanation: Cryptography is mainly categorized into two types; symmetric key cryptography and asymmetric key cryptography(public key cryptography). Symmetric key cryptography uses only one key for both encryption and decryption.

mcqs.question: What is the cipher text for the text “GREET HER”, if Caesar Cipher is used(key=3)?
mcqs.explanation: Caesar cipher is the substitution cipher, which belongs to classical cryptography. Cipher text will be obtained by replacing the plain text letters with letters three places further from them. If further letter is ‘z’, then process will circularly follows ‘a’.

mcqs.question: What is the cipher text for the message “TAKE ME TO THE PARTY”, id Rail Fence technique is used with two rows?
mcqs.explanation: Rail fence is the transposition technique, that belongs to classical cryptography. First the plain text is written in a sequence of diagonals with defined number of rows, then the cipher text is read off as a sequence of all the rows from starting to end.

mcqs.question: What are the two broad categories of symmetric key cryptography?
mcqs.explanation: Symmetric key cryptography has two types; classical and modern. Classical cryptography again divided into two types; transposition and substitution. Modern cryptography is of two types; stream cipher and block cipher.

mcqs.question: Which of the following algorithm does not belong to symmetric key ciphers?
mcqs.explanation: Diffie-Hellman is the first asymmetric cipher and well known for its logarithm computations. It is used at its best to transmit the secret key between users for further symmetric encryption of messages.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an advantage of symmetric cipher?

options.a: a) (N(N-1))/2 keys are required for N people
options.b: b) sharing secret key over communication channel
options.c: c) Brute force attack for small key size

mcqs.explanation: Quick encryption and decryption is done in symmetric key cryptography. Because, it uses less resources and cipher text length will be small or same as plain text. It encrypts huge amount of data quickly and provides confidentiality.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect about symmetric key cryptography?

options.a: a) It uses common key for both encryption and decryption
options.b: b) It is a secret key cryptography
options.c: c) It uses single fixed length key for each algorithm
options.d: d) Symmetric key can be combined with asymmetric key to achieve more security

mcqs.answer: c) It uses single fixed length key for each algorithm
mcqs.explanation: An algorithm can make use of number of random keys and the keys can be any size. If the key length is increased, then it will become difficult to crack the key.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of symmetric cipher?
mcqs.explanation: Symmetric key cryptography uses single key to encrypt and decrypt messages. If the secret key is shared through an unsecured channel, then there will be a chance for attacking the key.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an application of symmetric encryption algorithms.
mcqs.explanation: Unlike data security, cloud storage and user privacy, bitcoin uses elliptic-curve cryptography over symmetric key cryptography. Elliptic curve cryptography not only used for encryption, but also for digital signatures and random generators.

mcqs.question: Asymmetric ciphers are complex than symmetric ciphers.
mcqs.explanation: Asymmetric ciphers are much complex and slower than symmetric ciphers. Asymmetric ciphers have longer keys, which are more related to mathematics. As two keys are employed in asymmetric cipher, it is complex than symmetric ciphers.

links.context: This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Public Key Cryptography”.

mcqs.question: What are the two keys that are used in asymmetric key cryptography?

options.a: a) Secret key and private key
options.b: b) Private key and public key
options.c: c) Public key and secured key
options.d: d) Secured key and private key

mcqs.answer: b) Private key and public key
mcqs.explanation: In asymmetric key cryptography, each user needs to have 2 keys; one is public and another one is private key. Public key is used for encryption, private is used for decryption.

mcqs.question: Who are three discoverers of the RSA algorithm in public key cryptography?
mcqs.explanation: RSA algorithm is a public key algorithm, which was discovered at M.I.T in 1978. It is very strong but the only disadvantage is, it requires more key length in order to provide more security.

mcqs.question: What is the first public key cryptography algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Knapsack is the first public key algorithm, that was not that much secured and now it is not in use. Knapsack is the founding algorithm for further algorithms in public key cryptography.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a property of public key cryptography?

options.b: b) Every user has a unique private key
options.c: c) Public key can be same for number of users
options.d: d) Cannot deduce private key from public key

mcqs.answer: c) Public key can be same for number of users
mcqs.explanation: There will be a unique public key for every user, who publishes it. Public key prevents spoofing, by acting as the receiver. Sender uses the public key of the receiver to encrypt the message and the receiver will decrypt the message with his secret key.

mcqs.question: What are the types in schemes of public key encryption?

options.a: a) RSA, EIGamal, Elliptic curve cryptography

mcqs.answer: a) RSA, EIGamal, Elliptic curve cryptography
mcqs.explanation: RSA is the initial one and it achieves security using factoring of huge numbers. EIGamal uses numbers module p to strengthen the algorithm. Elliptic curve scheme uses discrete logarithms to achieve security.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is correct about RSA scheme in public key cryptography?

options.a: a) It is efficient for decryption
options.b: b) Lengthy keys are required for more security
options.c: c) It is not efficient for encryption

mcqs.answer: b) Lengthy keys are required for more security
mcqs.explanation: RSA schemes need at least 1024 bits in a key for providing good level of security. Symmetric key cryptography uses 128 bits. The more the key length, more the security in RSA, this is why RSA slows down the system.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an asymmetric key cryptography algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: RSA is named with the first letters of the discoverers (Rivest, Shamir, Aldleman). It uses lengthy keys for security and uses the concept of factoring large numbers to be secured.

mcqs.question: Which of the following doesn’t match as a property of elliptic curve cryptography?

options.c: c) Key length is larger than RSA

mcqs.answer: c) Key length is larger than RSA
mcqs.explanation: Elliptic curve cryptography is much faster and efficient than RSA algorithm. And keys are smaller in size, which are generated by elliptic curve equation.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the disadvantage of asymmetric cryptography?

options.a: a) No need of key distribution
options.d: d) Used to decrypt small messages

mcqs.answer: d) Used to decrypt small messages
mcqs.explanation: Public key cryptography cannot deal well with bulk messages. It uses very lengthy keys compared to symmetric key cryptography; this makes the system slow to proceed with bulk messages.

mcqs.question: A sender encrypts a message using recipient’s public key in public key cryptography?
mcqs.explanation: A sender can make use of pubic directory to acquire the public key of the recipient. After acquiring the public key of the receiver, sender will encrypt the message using receiver public key. If sender encrypts the message with his own secret key, then only the sender can decrypt it.

links.context:
This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Hash Functions”.

Essential Pre-read for this Topic: Security Services in Cryptography

mcqs.question: Which of the following equation is correct in case of hash function, where M = input, N = hash value, H = hash function?
mcqs.explanation: M is a block of data that is accepted by the hash function. Hash function(H) accepts the input and hash function will be performed. N is the fixed length of hash value of the block of input.

mcqs.question: What is/are the property(s) of a good hash function in case of producing outputs for set of inputs?

options.c: c) Apparently random and evenly distributed values
options.d: d) Evenly distributed but not apparently random values

mcqs.answer: c) Apparently random and evenly distributed values
mcqs.explanation: When a huge set of input blocks are given to a hash function, a good hash function will result in unique random values with no relation between them. At the same all the hash values will be equal that is fixed length.

mcqs.question: What is the core objective of the hash functions in producing hash values?
mcqs.explanation: Integrity means retrieving the lost data as soon as possible. Hash functions accomplish integrity, because, even one bit is changed in the data, it will result in a change of hash value with high probability.

mcqs.question: What is the name for hash functions that are used in security applications?
mcqs.explanation: The cryptographic hash function is an algorithm, which is used in security applications. It is computationally infeasible to attack the algorithm. Because it doesn’t allow the attacker to crack either of its properties, that are collision free property and one-way property.

mcqs.question: Which of the following application in which hash function is employed, refers hash value as message digest?
mcqs.explanation: The application “message authentication” is used to obtain the integrity of the message. Sender sends hash value of the message along with message, then receiver performs the same hash function on the message. If both the message digests are same, means, integrity is achieved.

mcqs.question: What is the other name for key hash function, which is used in message authentication?
mcqs.explanation: Message authentication code that is key hash function is mostly used in message authentication. This MAC function results a MAC value, by taking the input block of data and secret key. This MAC value is used to check whether data has changed or not.

mcqs.question: What is C<sub>i</sub>  in the bit-by-bit XOR hash function, that is C<sub>i</sub> = b<sub>i1</sub>  + b<sub>i2</sub>.….. + b<sub>im</sub>

options.a: a) Number of n bit blocks
options.b: b) i<sup>th</sup> bit of the hash code
options.c: c) i<sup>th</sup> bit in j<sup>th</sup> block

mcqs.answer: b) i<sup>th</sup> bit of the hash code
mcqs.explanation: “m” is the number of n-bit blocks in the input, bij is the ith bit in the jth block, ci is the ith bit of the hash code. Operation between the bits is exclusive OR and this operation is performed on every input block.

mcqs.question: When can we detect a collision if the hash values are same for two inputs, that is H(x) = H(y)?
mcqs.explanation: Hash function’s primary objective is to provide integrity. No two inputs should have the same hash value, which causes the collision. Collisions are undesirable in hash functions.

mcqs.question: What is the formula for pre-images of a given hash value, where data block length = b bits and hash code = n bits?
mcqs.explanation: In the hash value h = H(x), x is the preimage of the hash value. 2b-n formula finds the total number of possible collisions for a hash value. Here b > n and 2b is the total number of possible messages, 2n is the total number of possible hash values.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a basic property for employing hash function in practical applications?
mcqs.explanation: Hash function will produce fixed lengths of outputs and accepts any size of blocks as input. It is efficient to calculate. If these three requirements need to be met to implement hash function in practical applications.

mcqs.question: Which of the following property of the hash function makes the hash function strong?
mcqs.explanation: Hash function is referred as weak, when it only satisfies the Efficiency, preimage resistant, second image resistant, fixed length output, variable length input. It is referred as strong if it satisfies the collision resistant along with all of the above.

mcqs.question: Brute force attack does not concentrate on bit length of the hash value.
mcqs.explanation: The attacks that are on hash functions are brute force attack and crypt-analysis. Brute force attack mainly concentrates on the bit length of the hash function, whereas crypt-analysis concentrates on cryptographic algorithms.

links.context:
This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Digital Signatures”.

Essential Pre-read for this Topic: Security Services in Cryptography

mcqs.question: What can it be called, if an attacker determines the private key of the user, after breaking the signature scheme?
mcqs.explanation: Total break is finding private key and Universal forgery is finding signing algorithm. Selective forgery is doing forgery of signature for particular message. Atleast one message can have forgery signature.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a requirement of digital signatures?
mcqs.explanation: If a digital signature is computationally feasible, then it is very easy for a hacker to attack the signing scheme. He may forge the signature for the new message or change the signature for the present message.

mcqs.question: Who will be the involving parties in the direct digital signature scheme?

options.d: d) Source and destination and third party

mcqs.explanation: In general, there will be a third party, who authenticate the digital signatures. But there is no rule that everyone should believe the third party. So, the direct digital signature scheme involves sender and receiver. And receiver knows from where the message is coming using public key of the sender.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sentence is incorrect in case for digital signatures?

options.a: a) Signature key is of signing and public key for verification
options.b: b) Public key for verification and signature is for authentication
options.c: c) Signature key is for verification and public key for signing
options.d: d) Both signing and verification is done by public key

mcqs.answer: a) Signature key is of signing and public key for verification
mcqs.explanation: In digital signature, private key is the signature key, that is used to create digital signature. And this private key belongs to the signer. Public key belongs to the receiver who receives the message. These two keys are used in digital signature algorithm.

mcqs.question: What is the advantage of digital signing a hash instead of signing the entire data in RSA?

options.c: c) Time saving and computationally less expensive
options.d: d) Secured and less time requires

mcqs.answer: c) Time saving and computationally less expensive
mcqs.explanation: RSA uses expressions with exponential, that is modular exponentiation. So, it is difficult to let the large data be signed using modular exponentiation. Hash value of the message is small compared to the whole message. So, it saves time and computation power to use hash to be signed.

mcqs.question: Which of the following cannot be achieved by the digital signature in symmetric key encryption?
mcqs.explanation: Channel security is not in hands of digital signature, even the secret key is being transmitted between sender and receiver. Security of the message will be depending on the channel that is being used.

mcqs.question: Which of the following digital signature technique is based on elliptic curve cryptography?
mcqs.explanation: ECDSA stands for elliptic curve digital signature algorithm. ECDSA has huge acceptance, because it uses small key bit length, elliptic curve cryptography and secured.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a digital signature algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: SHA(secured hash function) is the hash algorithm which uses MD4 hash function. ECDSA, DSA and RSA – PSS are the three algorithms in digital signatures. ECDSA stands for elliptic curve digital signature algorithm, RSA – PSS is probabilistic signature scheme. DSA is digital signature algorithm.

mcqs.question: In which year, NIST proposed Elgamal algorithm in its new DSS(digital signature standard)?
mcqs.explanation: After RSA public key algorithm, ElGamal was introduced for digital signatures. But it is claimed by the government, that this algorithm is too slow, insecure, new and secret to meet the cyptographic standards.

mcqs.question: A signature function must be performed before the confidentiality function on a plain text in symmetric key digital signatures.
mcqs.explanation: Confidentiality function involves receivers public key for encryption, and private key for decryption. The sender cannot deceive the receiver when the digital signature function is inside. Because decryption of the message cannot be done by the sender without receiver’s private key. And the sender cannot change the digital signature.

title: 11. Computer Network MCQ on Point to Point Protocol & Error Detection

links.context: This set of Computer Networks Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Intrusion Detection Systems”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an advantage of anomaly detection?

options.a: a) Rules are easy to define
options.b: b) Custom protocols can be easily analyzed
options.c: c) The engine can scale as the rule set grows
options.d: d) Malicious activity that falls within normal usage patterns is detected

mcqs.answer: c) The engine can scale as the rule set grows
mcqs.explanation: Once a protocol has been built and a behavior defined, the engine can scale more quickly and easily than the signature-based model because a new signature does not have to be created for every attack and potential variant.

mcqs.question: A false positive can be defined as ________

options.a: a) An alert that indicates nefarious activity on a system that, upon further inspection, turns out to represent legitimate network traffic or behavior
options.b: b) An alert that indicates nefarious activity on a system that is not running on the network
options.c: c) The lack of an alert for nefarious activity
options.d: d) Both An alert that indicates nefarious activity on a system that, upon further inspection, turns out to represent legitimate network traffic or behavior and An alert that indicates nefarious activity on a system that is not running on the network

mcqs.answer: d) Both An alert that indicates nefarious activity on a system that, upon further inspection, turns out to represent legitimate network traffic or behavior and An alert that indicates nefarious activity on a system that is not running on the network
mcqs.explanation: A false positive is any alert that indicates nefarious activity on a system that, upon further inspection, turns out to represent legitimate network traffic or behavior.

mcqs.question: One of the most obvious places to put an IDS sensor is near the firewall. Where exactly in relation to the firewall is the most productive placement?

options.c: c) Both inside and outside the firewall
options.d: d) Neither inside the firewall nor outside the firewall.

mcqs.explanation: There are legitimate political, budgetary and research reasons to want to see all the “attacks” against your connection, but given the care and feeding any IDS requires, do yourself a favor and keep your NIDS sensors on the inside of the firewall.

mcqs.question: What is the purpose of a shadow honeypot?

options.a: a) To flag attacks against known vulnerabilities
options.b: b) To help reduce false positives in a signature-based IDS
options.c: c) To randomly check suspicious traffic identified by an anomaly detection system
options.d: d) To enhance the accuracy of a traditional honeypot

mcqs.answer: c) To randomly check suspicious traffic identified by an anomaly detection system
mcqs.explanation: “Shadow honeypots,” as researchers call them, share all the same characteristics of protected applications running on both the server and client side of a network and operate in conjunction with an ADS.

mcqs.question: At which two traffic layers do most commercial IDSes generate signatures?

options.a: a) Application layer and Network layer
options.b: b) Network layer and Session Layer
options.c: c) Transport layer and Application layer
options.d: d) Transport layer and Network layer

mcqs.answer: d) Transport layer and Network layer
mcqs.explanation: Most commercial IDSes generate signatures at the network and transport layers. These signatures are used to ensure that no malicious operation is contained in the traffic. Nemean generates signature at application and session layer.

mcqs.question: IDS follows a two-step process consisting of a passive component and an active component. Which of the following is part of the active component?

options.a: a) Inspection of password files to detect inadvisable passwords
options.b: b) Mechanisms put in place to reenact known methods of attack and record system responses
options.c: c) Inspection of system to detect policy violations
options.d: d) Inspection of configuration files to detect inadvisable settings

mcqs.answer: b) Mechanisms put in place to reenact known methods of attack and record system responses
mcqs.explanation: Secondary components of mechanism are set in place to reenact known methods of attack and to record system responses. In passive components, the system I designed just to record the system’s responses in case of an intrusion.

mcqs.question: When discussing IDS/IPS, what is a signature?

options.a: a) An electronic signature used to authenticate the identity of a user on the network
options.c: c) It refers to “normal,” baseline network behavior
options.d: d) It is used to authorize the users on a network
